Namespace: mne · Library: FIFF Library · Source: fiff/fiff_coord_trans_set.h #include <mne/fiff/fiff_coord_trans_set.h> class mne::FiffCoordTransSet The chain of transforms from MEG head coordinates to MNI and FreeSurfer Talairach coordinates. Head -> surface RAS (the FreeSurfer MRI frame) comes from the coregistration, surface RAS -> scanner RAS from the centre (c_ras) of the subject's MRI, scanner RAS -> MNI Talairach from mri/transforms/talairach.xfm, and MNI -> FreeSurfer Talairach from the fixed Brett approximations MNE-C uses (one matrix above and one below the AC-PC plane). Empty transforms mark links that are not known. src/examples/ex_fiff_api/main.cpp // Head -> MRI -> RAS -> MNI Talairach -> Talairach, as mne_analyze reports a picked location FiffCoordTransSet chain; chain.read((dir + "/../../subjects/sample/mri/brain-neuromag/sets/COR.fif").toStdString()); // surface RAS -> RAS of the MRI set chain.read((dir + "/all-trans.fif").toStdString()); // the coregistration, head -> MRI chain.addTalairach(MNE_TALAIRACH_XFM); // the subject's mri/transforms/talairach.xfm MatrixX3f headPoints(1, 3); headPoints << 0.03f, -0.02f, 0.12f; const MatrixX3f mni = chain.headToMni(headPoints); const MatrixX3f talairach = chain.mniToTalairach(mni);

Mirrors the original fiffDataRefRec exactly: a 24-byte record made of two std::int32_t (type, endianness flag) followed by two std::int64_t (payload size in bytes, byte offset into the external file). The points come in the order of mne.channels.make_dig_montage: the cardinal points (LPA, nasion, RPA), HPI coils, head shape points, then the EEG electrodes. Reads the coordinates.xml of an EGI MFF recording, as mne.channels.read_dig_egi does. Sensors of type 0 become EEG electrodes named "EEG <number>", the reference (type 1) is numbered after the electrodes before it, and the nasion and periauricular points (type 2) become the cardinal points. Unlike mne.channels.read_dig_egi, which keeps the file's centimetres as if they were metres, the positions are converted to metres (as mne.io.read_raw_egi does). Namespace: mne · Library: FIFF Library · Source: fiff/fiff_dir_node.h #include <mne/fiff/fiff_dir_node.h> class mne::FiffDirNode Recursive FIFF block-tree node: block kind, block ID, directly contained directory entries and child sub-blocks. Each node corresponds to one FIFFB_BLOCK_START ... FIFFB_BLOCK_END pair in the on-disk tag stream. The full tree is built once by FiffStream::make_dir_tree after the directory tag is parsed, and is then traversed by every higher-level reader (FiffInfo, FiffRawData, FiffEvoked, FiffCov, ...) via dir_tree_find. Namespace: mne · Library: FIFF Library · Source: fiff/fiff_epochs.h Python equivalent mne.Epochs in MNE-Python. #include <mne/fiff/fiff_epochs.h> class mne::FiffEpochs Static helpers that cut continuous data into fixed-length epochs, concatenate and average them. Stateless; operates on data matrices. Counterpart of mne.make_fixed_length_epochs and mne.concatenate_epochs in MNE-Python. src/examples/ex_fiff_structure/main.cpp FiffRawData raw(rawPath.toStdString()); MatrixXd data; MatrixXd times; ok &= raw.read_raw_segment(data, times); // all 6007 samples const double sfreq = raw.info.sfreq; const std::vector<FiffEpochData> epochs = FiffEpochs::makeFixedLengthEpochs(data, sfreq, 2.0, 0.5); // 2 s, 0.5 s overlap const FiffEvoked average = FiffEpochs::averageEpochs(epochs, sfreq);

Create fixed-length epochs from continuous data. Segments the data matrix into non-overlapping (or overlapping) epochs of the specified duration. Parameters: matData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Continuous data (n_channels × n_times). dSFreq : double Sampling frequency in Hz. dDuration : double Epoch duration in seconds. dOverlap : double Overlap between epochs in seconds (default 0.0). bDropLast : bool Drop the last epoch if it's shorter than duration (default true). Returns: std::vector< FiffEpochData > — List of epoch data structures.

Concatenate multiple epoch sets into a single list. Parameters: epochSets : const std::vector< std::vector< FiffEpochData > > & List of epoch sets to concatenate. Returns: std::vector< FiffEpochData > — Combined list of all epochs.

Compute the average (evoked response) across epochs. All epochs must have the same dimensions. Returns a FiffEvoked with data, nave, times, and aspect_kind populated. Parameters: epochs : const std::vector< FiffEpochData > & List of epochs. dSFreq : double Sampling frequency in Hz (used to compute times vector). comment : const std::string & Comment string for the evoked (default "Average"). Returns: FiffEvoked — FiffEvoked with averaged data and metadata.

Extract data matrices from epoch structures. Convenience method to get a list of data matrices from epoch structures, suitable for use with CSP, SPoC, SSD, etc. Parameters: epochs : const std::vector< FiffEpochData > & List of epoch data. Returns: std::vector< Eigen::MatrixXd > — List of data matrices (n_channels × n_times).

Namespace: mne · Library: FIFF Library · Source: fiff/fiff_events.h #include <mne/fiff/fiff_events.h> class mne::FiffEvents FIFF event list: (sample, prev, new) integer triples with read / write / detect / filter helpers. On-disk representation matches mne.io.write.write_events output and the -eve.fif files consumed by mne.read_events; the detection path mirrors mne.find_events. Used by FiffEpochs and the batch-averaging path in FiffEvokedSet to drive epoch extraction. src/examples/ex_fiff_api/main.cpp const FiffEvents events = FiffEvents::find_events(raw, "STI 014").value(); // rising edges, like mne.find_events const std::string eventPath = tmp.filePath("sample-eve.fif").toStdString(); const bool eventsWritten = events.write(eventPath).has_value(); FiffEvents eventsBack(eventPath); // mne.read_events reads this file too
Constructs an event list. Parameters: events : Eigen::MatrixXi Events, one row [sample, before, after] each.
Reads an event file like read(); throws Error if it cannot. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The event file.

Writes the events, like mne.write_events: to FIFF if the name holds ".fif", as text otherwise. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The file. sfreq : float Sampling frequency for the time column of a text file; 0 writes zeros. Returns: Expected< void > — Nothing, or why the file cannot be written.

Writes the events to a FIFF file. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The FIFF file. Returns: Expected< void > — Nothing, or why the file cannot be written: Format if there are no events, Io otherwise.

Writes the events as text, one "sample time before after" line each, as MNE-C does. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The text file. sfreq : float Sampling frequency for the time column; 0 writes zeros. Returns: Expected< void > — Nothing, or why the file cannot be written (Io).
Returns: int — The number of events.
Returns: bool — Whether there is no event.

Selects events by code, like mne.pick_events. Parameters: include : const std::vector< int > & Codes to keep; if none, all codes except \p exclude are kept. exclude : const std::vector< int > & Codes to drop when include is empty. step : bool Also match the code before the step (column 1). Returns: FiffEvents — The selected events in their original order.

Replaces codes in both code columns by a new one, like mne.merge_events. Parameters: ids : const std::vector< int > & Codes to replace. new_id : int The new code. replace_events : bool If false, the original events are kept as well, sorted by row. Returns: FiffEvents — The merged events.

Counts the events per code (column 2), like mne.count_events. Parameters: ids : const std::vector< int > & Codes to report (0 if absent); if none, every code that occurs. Returns: std::map< int, int > — The number of events with each code.

Reads an event file, like mne.read_events: a FIFF file if its name holds ".fif", text otherwise. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The event file. Returns: Expected< FiffEvents > — The events, or why the file cannot be read.

Reads the event list of a FIFF file. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The FIFF file. Returns: Expected< FiffEvents > — The events, or why the file cannot be read: Io if it cannot be opened, NotFound if it holds no event list.

Reads a text event file: one event per line as "sample [time] before after"; lines starting with '' or '#' are comments. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The text file. Returns: Expected< FiffEvents > — The events, or why the file cannot be read: Io if it cannot be opened, Format if a line does not start with a sample number.

Finds the trigger events of a stimulus channel, like mne.find_events. Parameters: raw : const FiffRawData & The recording. stim_channel : std::string_view Name of the stimulus channel; matched as same_channel() does ("STI014" finds "STI 014"). mask : unsigned int Bits of the channel value that count. leading_edge : bool Only changes from 0 to a non-zero value, rather than every change. Returns: Expected< FiffEvents > — The events, which may be none, or why there are none: NotFound if the channel is missing, Io if its data cannot be read.

Checks whether an event matches an averaging category, as MNE-C's mne_process_raw does. Parameters: cat : const AverageCategory & The category. events : const Eigen::MatrixXi & Events, one row [sample, before, after] each. event_idx : int Row of the event. Returns: bool — Whether the event matches, including the category's conditions on the events around it.

Concatenates the events of consecutive recordings, like mne.concatenate_events. Parameters: events : const std::vector< FiffEvents > & Events of each recording. first_samps : const std::vector< int > & First sample of each recording. last_samps : const std::vector< int > & Last sample of each recording. Returns: FiffEvents — Events on the sample axis of the concatenated recording (none if the list lengths differ).

Find the samples where all stimulus channels change at once, like mne.find_stim_steps. Parameters: stim_data : const Eigen::MatrixXi & Stimulus channel data (channels x samples); steps carry the values of the first row. first_samp : int Sample number of the first column. pad_start : std::optional< int > If set, a step from this value at sample 0 is added when the data start elsewhere. pad_stop : std::optional< int > If set, a step to this value after the last sample is added. merge : int Merge steps at most |merge| samples apart (> 0: into the later, < 0: into the earlier). Returns: FiffEvents — Steps as [sample, value before, value after].

Events at regular intervals, like mne.make_fixed_length_events. Parameters: raw : const FiffRawData & The recording. id : int Event code. start : double First event time in s. stop : double Time in s after which no event may start (negative: end of the recording). duration : double Duration of each segment in s. first_samp : bool Whether times count from the recording's first sample (true) or from 0. overlap : double Overlap of consecutive segments in s, 0 <= overlap < duration. Returns: FiffEvents — The events (empty if none fit or the overlap is invalid).

Understand the method The MEG/EEG Processing Workflow › Epoching and Evoked Data The MEG/EEG Processing Workflow › Off-Line Averaging Command-line tools mne_process_raw Use the API MNEEpochDataList::readEpochs()::computeAverage() FiffEvoked FiffEvokedSet Run an example Average epochs into an evoked responseStart here Read epochs from a raw recording List the conditions of an evoked file class mne::FiffEvokedSet Set of FiffEvoked instances sharing one FiffInfo, plus channel-picking and compensation helpers. The on-disk shape of a *-ave.fif: one FiffInfo and one FiffEvoked per FIFFB_EVOKED block (one per averaging condition). Conversion utilities pick channels and shift compensation state across the whole set in lock-step. src/examples/ex_fiff_api/main.cpp FiffEvokedSet evokedSet((dir + "/sample_audvis-ave.fif").toStdU16String()); // all conditions of an -ave.fif file const FiffEvoked& leftAuditory = evokedSet.evoked[0];
Constructs a fiff evoked data set.

Reads evoked data sets of a FIFF file, like read(); throws Error if it cannot. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The file. conditions : const std::vector< FiffEvoked::Condition > & Indices or comments of the averages to read, in this order; empty reads all. baseline : const FiffEvoked::Baseline & Interval to subtract the mean of, or none for no baseline correction. proj : bool Apply the SSP projectors of the file.
Copy constructor. Parameters: p_FiffEvokedSet : const FiffEvokedSet & Fiff evoked data set which should be copied.

Copy assignment. Every member has value semantics, so the compiler-generated member-wise assignment is correct. It is declared explicitly because declaring a copy constructor and/or a destructor deprecates the implicitly generated one. Parameters: other : const FiffEvokedSet & Object to assign from. Returns: FiffEvokedSet & — reference to this object.
Destroys the fiff evoked data set.

fiff_pick_channels_evoked Pick desired channels from evoked-response data Parameters: include : const StringList & Channels to include (if empty, include all available). exclude : const StringList & Channels to exclude (if empty, do not exclude any). Returns: FiffEvokedSet — the desired fiff evoked data set.

mne_compensate_to Changes the CTF gradient compensation grade of all evoked responses in place. Parameters: to : fiff_int_t Desired compensation grade. Returns: bool — true if the data were changed, false if they already had that grade or it is not available.
fiff_find_evoked Find evoked data sets Parameters: p_FiffEvokedSet : const FiffEvokedSet & The read evoked data set. Returns: bool — true when any set was found, false otherwise.
Writes the evoked data sets to a FIFF file, like mne.write_evokeds. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The file. Returns: Expected< void > — Nothing, or why the file cannot be written.

Reads evoked data sets of a FIFF file in one pass, like mne.read_evokeds. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The file. conditions : const std::vector< FiffEvoked::Condition > & Indices or comments of the averages to read, in this order; empty reads all. baseline : const FiffEvoked::Baseline & Interval to subtract the mean of, or none for no baseline correction. proj : bool Apply the SSP projectors of the file. Returns: Expected< FiffEvokedSet > — The evoked data sets, or why the file does not hold them.

Compute a grand average across multiple evoked data sets (mne.grand_average with interpolate_bads=False, drop_bads=True). For each category, channels marked bad in any set are dropped, the common channels are kept and the sets are combined with equal weights. nave is set to the number of sets and the comment to "Grand average (n = N)". Parameters: evokedSets : const std::vector< FiffEvokedSet > & List of evoked data sets to combine. Returns: FiffEvokedSet — The grand-average evoked set, or an empty set if input is empty.

Compute epoch-based averages from raw data according to an averaging description. For each category in the description, matching events are epoched from the raw data, artifact-rejected, baseline-corrected, and averaged into a FiffEvoked entry. Parameters: raw : const FiffRawData & The raw data. desc : const AverageDescription & The averaging description (categories, rejection, etc.). events : const Eigen::MatrixXi & Event matrix (nEvents x 3): [sample, from, to]. log : std::string & Processing log output. Returns: FiffEvokedSet — FiffEvokedSet containing one FiffEvoked per category, or empty set on failure.

Check whether an epoch passes artifact rejection criteria. Parameters: epoch : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Epoch data (nChannels x nSamples). info : const FiffInfo & Channel info. bads : const StringList & List of bad channel names. rej : const RejectionParams & Rejection parameters. reason : std::string & Rejection reason string (set only when rejected). Returns: bool — true if epoch is clean (not rejected).

Subtract baseline from each channel of an epoch. For each row (channel), the mean of the samples in [bminSamp, bminSamp+nBase) is subtracted. Parameters: epoch : Eigen::MatrixXd & Data matrix (channels x samples) to correct in-place. bminSamp : int First baseline sample (clamped to 0). bmaxSamp : int Last baseline sample (clamped to epoch length - 1).

Reads one evoked data set, like read(); throws Error if it cannot. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The file. condition : const Condition & Index of the data set, or its comment together with kind. baseline : const Baseline & Interval to subtract the mean of, or none for no baseline correction. proj : bool Apply the SSP projectors of the file. kind : fiff_int_t FIFFV_ASPECT_AVERAGE or FIFFV_ASPECT_STD_ERR; selects among sets of the same comment.
Copy constructor. Parameters: p_FiffEvoked : const FiffEvoked & Fiff evoked data which should be copied.

Copy assignment. Every member has value semantics, so the compiler-generated member-wise assignment is correct. Returns: FiffEvoked & — reference to this object.
Returns list of channel names stored in fiff info -> this is to stay consistent with python. Returns: const StringList & — List of channel names.

Provides the python Evoked string formatted aspect_kind, which is stored in kind: "average" <-> FIFFV_ASPECT_AVERAGE, "standard_error" <-> FIFFV_ASPECT_STD_ERR or "unknown". Returns: std::string — string formatted aspect_kind.
Returns whether FiffEvoked is empty. Returns: bool — true if is empty, false otherwise.

fiff_pick_channels_evoked Pick desired channels from evoked-response data Parameters: include : const StringList & Channels to include (if empty, include all available). exclude : const StringList & Channels to exclude (if empty, do not exclude any). Returns: FiffEvoked — the desired fiff evoked data.
Set a new fiff measurement info. Parameters: p_info : const FiffInfo & Info to set. applyProj : bool Apply SSP projection vectors (optional, default = true).

Inputs a new data set and recalculates the average. This function also iterates the nave parameter by one. Parameters: newData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & the new data set which is to be added to the current average. Returns: FiffEvoked & — the updated FiffEvoked.
Applies baseline correction to the evoked data. Parameters: p_baseline : std::pair< float, float > & time definition of the baseline in seconds [from, to].

Reads one evoked data set of a FIFF file, like mne.read_evokeds. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The file. condition : const Condition & Index of the data set, or its comment together with kind. baseline : const Baseline & Interval to subtract the mean of, or none for no baseline correction. proj : bool Apply the SSP projectors of the file. kind : fiff_int_t FIFFV_ASPECT_AVERAGE or FIFFV_ASPECT_STD_ERR; selects among sets of the same comment. Returns: Expected< FiffEvoked > — The evoked data, or why the file holds none matching condition.

Merges evoked data by weighted addition or subtraction (mne.combine_evoked). All data sets must have the same channels and time instants. The result carries the union of the bad channels, the weighted sum of the data, a comment such as "0.474 × A + 0.526 × B" and nave = 1 / sum(w_i^2 / nave_i), rounded to an integer as required by the FIFF format. Namespace: mne · Library: FIFF Library · Source: fiff/fiff_tag.h #include <mne/fiff/fiff_tag.h> class mne::FiffTag FIFF tag: 16-byte header (kind, type, size, next) plus payload, with typed decoders for every FIFFT_* type. Holds the four header fields exactly as stored on disk and the raw payload bytes. Decoders convert the payload to the appropriate C++ representation: scalars via to_int / to_float / to_double, dense and sparse matrices via to_float_matrix / to_sparse_float_matrix, and the structured FIFF records into their class wrappers (to_fiff_id, to_coord_trans, to_ch_info, to_dig_point, to_dir_entry, ...). Namespace: mne · Library: FreeSurfer Library · Source: fs/fs_colortable.h #include <mne/fs/fs_colortable.h> class mne::FsColortable FreeSurfer colour lookup table: region name + RGBA + packed label, indexed by entry. Namespace: mne · Library: FreeSurfer Library · Source: fs/fs_label_utils.h Python equivalent mne.grow_labels / mne.split_label / mne.stc_to_label in MNE-Python. #include <mne/fs/fs_label_utils.h> class mne::FsLabelUtils Stateless utilities that grow, split and convert FsLabel objects on a FreeSurfer triangular surface. All operations take an FsSurface as the topology source and treat its triangle faces as the vertex adjacency graph. The helpers are static because labels carry their own state and the surface is supplied per call, mirroring the function-based API used by MNE-Python. src/examples/ex_fs/main.cpp const FsLabel grown = FsLabelUtils::growLabel(v1, white, 1); // add the one-ring neighbours const std::vector<FsLabel> parts = FsLabelUtils::splitLabel(v1, white);

Grow a label by expanding along the surface mesh. Starting from the seed vertices in the label, expands outward by nSteps along surface edges (breadth-first). Parameters: label : const FsLabel & The seed label to grow from. surface : const FsSurface & The surface providing vertex adjacency. nSteps : int Number of expansion steps. Returns: FsLabel — Grown label containing original + expanded vertices.

Grow a circular label around seed vertices, as mne.grow_labels does for one seed set. Vertices within extentMm geodesic distance along the mesh edges are included, following mne's label growing (a distance found later is lowered but not propagated again). The label values are the distances in whole millimetres, as in MNE-Python. Parameters: surface : const FsSurface & Surface of the hemisphere. seeds : std::span< const int > Seed vertices. extentMm : double Maximum geodesic distance in mm. hemi : int Hemisphere (0 = lh, 1 = rh). name : const std::string & Label name; "-lh" / "-rh" is appended unless present. Returns: FsLabel — The grown label, vertices ascending.

Split a label into connected components. Namespace: mne · Library: FreeSurfer Library · Source: fs/fs_label.h Python equivalent mne.read_label in MNE-Python. #include <mne/fs/fs_label.h> class mne::FsLabel A FreeSurfer/MNE surface label: per-vertex indices, Tk-RAS positions and scalar values for one hemisphere. Wraps the parsed contents of a .label file or an in-memory label constructed programmatically (e.g. by thresholding a source estimate via FsLabelUtils::stcToLabel). Vertex indices reference the matching FsSurface for the same subject and hemisphere; positions are the Tk-surface RAS coordinates copied from that surface; values are the per-vertex scalar payload (statistic, time, weight). Hemisphere is encoded with the FreeSurfer convention {0 = lh, 1 = rh}. src/examples/ex_fs/main.cpp FsLabel v1; FsLabel::read((subjectsDir + "/sample/label/lh.V1.label").toStdU16String(), v1);

Namespace: mne · Library: FreeSurfer Library · Source: fs/fs_surfaceset.h #include <mne/fs/fs_surfaceset.h> class mne::FsSurfaceSet Container holding the lh and/or rh FsSurface for one subject and one surface kind. The set is keyed on the hemisphere id (0 = lh, 1 = rh) so callers can do set[0] / set[1] or iterate over set.data(). Namespace: mne · Source: src/libs/mne/fwd The Forward library computes MEG and EEG forward solutions — the mapping from source currents in the brain to sensor measurements. It supports BEM (Boundary Element Method) models with constant or linear collocation, multi-layer concentric-sphere EEG head models, and arbitrary coil/electrode configurations. The library also provides sensor-to-surface field mapping for topographic interpolation. All classes reside in the mne_fwd namespace.

Class Description MNE-Python MNE-C ComputeFwd Main worker that orchestrates forward solution computation: initialises source space, BEM/sphere model, coils, and dispatches computation to threads mne.make_forward_solution() Forward solver kernel ComputeFwdSettings Container for all forward computation parameters: source space path, BEM path, EEG model, coordinate frame — Configuration struct

ComputeFwd is the worker/factory that takes a ComputeFwdSettings, initialises all required data structures (coil definitions, BEM or sphere model, source spaces, compensation data, coordinate transforms) and assembles the MEG/EEG lead-field matrix G one dipole column at a time. Surfaces are stored from outermost (scalp) to innermost (inner skull) and owned by this object; the solution matrix is built once by fwd_bem_compute_solution and then re-used for every source. Refactored from the MNE-C fwdBemModel / fwdBemModelRec struct (fwd_types.h). Raw C-style arrays were replaced with Eigen types; surface ownership is managed through std::unique_ptr. src/examples/ex_fwd_api/main.cpp auto bem = FwdBemModel::fwd_bem_load_homog_surface((data + "/subjects/sample/bem/sample-5120-bem.fif").toStdU16String()); bem->fwd_bem_load_recompute_solution((data + "/subjects/sample/bem/sample-5120-bem-sol.fif").toStdU16String(), FWD_BEM_LINEAR_COLL, 0); bem->fwd_bem_set_head_mri_t(FiffCoordTrans((data + "/MEG/sample/all-trans.fif").toStdU16String(), FIFFV_COORD_MRI, FIFFV_COORD_HEAD)); bem->fwd_bem_specify_coils(coils.get()); // stores a FwdBemSolution per coil set in coils->user_data VectorXf B(coils->ncoil()); FwdBemModel::fwd_bem_field(rd, Q, *coils, B, bem.get()); // T per A m
Constructs an empty BEM model. All Eigen containers are left at size zero; scalar members are set to safe defaults (nsurf = 0, nsol = 0, bem_method = FWD_BEM_UNKNOWN).
Destroys the BEM model. FsSurface ownership is released automatically via std::unique_ptr. The solution matrix is freed by fwd_bem_free_solution().
Release the potential solution matrix and associated workspace. Resets solution, v0, sol_name, nsol, and bem_method to their default (empty / unknown) state.
Find a surface of the given kind in this BEM model. Parameters: kind : int FsSurface ID to look for. Returns: *MNESurface ** — Non-owning pointer to the surface, or nullptr if not found.

Namespace: mne · Source: src/libs/mne/ieeg The mne_ieeg library (mne_ieeg namespace) holds what is specific to intracranial recordings, sEEG depth leads and ECoG strips and grids: the implantation (contacts grouped into leads), bipolar re-referencing along the leads, and the mapping of contact values onto the cortical surface. target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE mne_ieeg) Dependencies: mne_bids, mne_base, Qt6::Core, Eigen3. Rendering lives in the 3-D view of mne_viz_qt (ElectrodeObject), which takes the leads as shown in mne_inspect.

Class / Struct Header Description IeegImplantation ieeg/ieeg_implantation.h Contacts and the leads they form; BIDS iEEG *_electrodes.tsv reader IeegContact ieeg/ieeg_implantation.h One contact: name, position (m), lead IeegLead ieeg/ieeg_implantation.h One depth lead, strip or grid: contacts in order along it, grid shape IeegReference ieeg/ieeg_reference.h Bipolar pairs along leads and their montage matrix IeegBipolarPair ieeg/ieeg_reference.h One derivation: anode, cathode, name, midpoint IeegSurfaceMap ieeg/ieeg_surface_map.h Vertices x contacts weights painting contact values onto a surface

Units and frame. Positions are in metres. IeegImplantation::coordinateSystem() names their frame (e.g. ACPC); the library does not transform between frames. Leads from names. Without a BIDS group, a contact belongs to the lead named like the contact without its trailing number (LA1, LA10 → LA), ordered by that number. A' (the prime marks the other hemisphere) never merges with A. Lead type. BIDS type or a dimension of more than one row and column decides; otherwise contacts closer than 6 mm make a depth lead, others a strip. No guessing of units. IeegImplantation::readBids refuses an *_electrodes.tsv without a matching *_coordsystem.json or with units other than m, cm or mm. MNE-BIDS infers n/a units from the coordinate magnitudes instead; for intracranial contacts a wrong guess moves them by a factor of ten.

Group contacts into leads. A contact without a lead name belongs to the lead named like the contact without its trailing number (LA1, LA10 -> LA; A'1 stays apart from A1, the prime marking the other hemisphere). Within a lead, contacts are ordered by that number. A lead whose closest neighbouring contacts are less than kMaxDepthSpacing apart is a depth lead, others are strips. Read a BIDS iEEG *_electrodes.tsv. Units and the coordinate system come from the *_coordsystem.json in the same folder that shares the longest name prefix; without one the file is refused, since the units are then unknown. Contacts without coordinates are skipped. The group column assigns leads and the dimension column ("[4x8]") the grid shape; a type naming depth, strip or grid sets the lead type. Otherwise names and spacing decide, as in the constructor. Pair each contact with its next neighbour on the same lead: along a depth lead or strip, and along the rows and then the columns of a grid with a known shape. The contact earlier along the lead is the anode, so a depth lead gives LA1-LA2, LA2-LA3, … Parameters: implantation : const IeegImplantation & Contacts and leads. Returns: std::vector< IeegBipolarPair > — The derivations, lead by lead.

Montage matrix of the derivations: bipolar data = M * contact data. Parameters: pairs : const std::vector< IeegBipolarPair > & Derivations. contactCount : int Number of contacts, the columns of M. Returns: Eigen::SparseMatrix< double > — Sparse pairs x contacts matrix, +1 at the anode and -1 at the cathode of each row.

At inference time, InvCMNE::compute() runs dSPM to obtain a base source estimate, then applies the ONNX-exported LSTM model sample-by-sample to produce a spatiotemporally refined CMNE result. Namespace: mne · Library: Inverse Library · Source: inv/beamformer/inv_beamformer_compute.h #include <mne/inv/inv_beamformer_compute.h> class mne::InvBeamformerCompute Shared computation routines used by both LCMV and DICS beamformers. All methods are static — no state is kept between calls. Core beamformer math.

Compute beamformer spatial filter weights from a leadfield and data covariance (or CSD). This implements the core LCMV/DICS algorithm: Regularize and invert covariance Reshape leadfield per source (n_channels x n_orient) Optionally reduce leadfield rank Select orientation (max-power, normal, or keep all) Invert denominator G^T Cm^{-1} G Apply weight normalization Parameters: G : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Leadfield matrix (n_channels, n_sources * n_orient). Cm : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Data covariance or CSD matrix (n_channels, n_channels). Real-valued. reg : double Regularization parameter (fraction of trace to add, e.g. 0.05). nOrient : int Orientations per source: 1 (fixed) or 3 (free). weightNorm : BeamformerWeightNorm Weight normalization strategy. pickOri : BeamformerPickOri Orientation selection mode. reduceRank : bool If true, reduce leadfield rank by 1 (for MEG sphere models). invMethod : BeamformerInversion Denominator inversion strategy (matrix or scalar). nn : const Eigen::MatrixX3d & Source normals (n_sources, 3). Used for max-power sign alignment. W : Eigen::MatrixXd & Output spatial filter weights (n_sources * n_orient_out, n_channels). maxPowerOri : Eigen::MatrixX3d & Output max-power orientations (n_sources, 3). Empty if not max-power. Returns: bool — True on success.

documents.t: Compute source power from spatial filter weights and a data covariance / CSD matrix. power_i = trace(W_i Cm W_i^T) Parameters: Cm : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Data covariance or CSD (n_channels, n_channels). W : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Spatial filter weights (n_sources * n_orient, n_channels). nOrient : int Orientations per source. Returns: Eigen::VectorXd — Source power vector (n_sources).

Symmetric matrix power: X^p via eigendecomposition. Parameters: X : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Symmetric matrix. p : double Power exponent (e.g. -1, -0.5). reduceRank : bool Drop smallest eigenvalue before exponentiating. Returns: Eigen::MatrixXd — X^p.

Namespace: mne · Library: Inverse Library · Source: inv/inv_connectivity.h #include <mne/inv/inv_connectivity.h> struct mne::InvConnectivity Stores a pairwise connectivity measure between source locations (grid points, sEEG contacts, etc.). The matrix is [N x N] where N equals the number of sources in the parent InvSourceEstimate. Each InvConnectivity instance represents one metric in one frequency band and time window. For frequency-resolved connectivity, add one entry per band to the parent's connectivity vector. This struct is intentionally lightweight and self-contained — it does not depend on the connectivity library. Application code can populate it from Network::connectivity_matrix(). Pairwise source connectivity matrix with measure, directionality, and frequency/time metadata. src/examples/ex_inv_api/main.cpp InvSourceEstimate layered = stc; InvFocalDipole dipole; // an off-grid ECD result alongside the grid dipole.position = Vector3f(0.01f, -0.08f, 0.03f); dipole.moment = Vector3f(0.0f, 0.0f, 20e-9f); dipole.goodness = 0.9f; layered.focalDipoles.push_back(dipole); InvSourceCoupling pair; // two grid sources that move together pair.gridIndices = {0, 1}; pair.moments = {Vector3d::UnitZ(), Vector3d::UnitZ()}; pair.correlations = Matrix2d{{1.0, 0.8}, {0.8, 1.0}}; layered.couplings.push_back(pair); InvConnectivity coherence; // a source-space connectivity layer coherence.measure = "coh"; coherence.matrix = Matrix2d{{1.0, 0.4}, {0.4, 1.0}}; coherence.fmin = 8.0f; coherence.fmax = 12.0f; layered.connectivity.push_back(coherence); InvTokenizeOptions options; // at most 5 sources and 10 samples; values travel as float options.maxSources = 5; options.maxTimePoints = 10; const std::vector<InvToken> tokens = tokenize(layered, options); const InvSourceEstimate fromTokenStream = fromTokens(tokens);

Namespace: mne · Library: Inverse Library Module This page documents a header-level module — a collection of free functions that share an algorithmic topic. There is no enclosing C++ class; the functions live directly in the library namespace. Python equivalent mne.minimum_norm.apply_inverse_epochs / apply_inverse_raw / apply_inverse_cov in MNE-Python. #include <mne/inv/inv_convenience.h> SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause Copyright (c) 2026 MNE-CPP Authors. apply_inverse_* / compute_source_psd helpers. Free functions in this header glue together the lower-level mne_inv classes so users can match the MNE-Python ergonomics: mne::apply_inverse_epochs applies a precomputed inverse operator across an epoch list, apply_inverse_raw streams raw data through the kernel, estimate_snr returns the whitened-data SNR trace from an evoked + inverse pair, compute_whitener produces the diagonal whitener from a noise covariance, and compute_source_psd / compute_source_band_power run Welch-based spectral analysis directly on InvSourceEstimate output. All methods are headers-only orchestration on top of InvMinimumNorm and the underlying FIFF / MNE primitives. src/examples/ex_inv_api/main.cpp // Whitened data and a gain per nAm make the noise level 1, as mne.inverse_sparse.mixed_norm does. const auto [whitener, rank] = compute_whitener(inverse.noise_cov); // rank 360: 364 channels minus 4 projectors const MNEForwardSolution fixedFwd = MNEForwardSolution(fwdPath, {.force_fixed = true, .surf_ori = true}).pick_regions({v1}).pick_channels(inverse.noise_cov.names); const MatrixXd gain = whitener * fixedFwd.sol.data * 1e-9; const MatrixXd measured = whitener * evoked.pick_channels(inverse.noise_cov.names).data.middleCols(170, 40); // 83-148 ms const double alphaMax = (gain.transpose() * measured).rowwise().norm().maxCoeff(); const InvMxneResult mxne = InvMxne::compute(gain, measured, 0.5 * alphaMax, 1000, 1e-10);

For each epoch (data matrix), applies the minimum norm inverse and returns a list of source estimates. This is the equivalent of MNE-Python's mne.minimum_norm.apply_inverse_epochs(). documents.t: [FiffEvoked](/docs/api/fiff/fiff-evoked) apply_forward(const [MNEForwardSolution](/docs/api/mne/mne-forward-solution) & fwd, const [InvSourceEstimate](/docs/api/inv/inv-source-estimate) & stc, const [FiffInfo](/docs/api/fiff/fiff-info) & info); Project a source estimate to the sensors, as mne.apply_forward. A free-orientation forward is first converted to fixed orientation along the (patch-averaged) cortical normals. The source estimate rows are matched to forward columns by vertex number per hemisphere (stc.nVerticesLh splits lh and rh); a vertex the forward lacks is an error. A forward without source spaces is used column by column. The evoked carries the forward's channels taken from info. Parameters: fwd : const MNEForwardSolution & Forward solution; its channels must all be in info. stc : const InvSourceEstimate & Source estimate with one row per source. info : const FiffInfo & Measurement info supplying the channel descriptions. Returns: FiffEvoked — Simulated evoked data, empty on error.

std::pair< Eigen::VectorXd, Eigen::VectorXd > estimate_snr(const [FiffEvoked](/docs/api/fiff/fiff-evoked) & evoked, const [MNEInverseOperator](/docs/api/mne/mne-inverse-operator) & inverse); Estimate the SNR of evoked data as a function of time. Equivalent of MNE-Python's mne.minimum_norm.estimate_snr(): snr is the global field power of the whitened data, snrEst the largest regularization 1/sqrt(lambda2) whose prediction error passes a chi^2 test at p = 0.001 (0 where snr <= 1). Parameters: evoked : const FiffEvoked & Evoked data. inverse : const MNEInverseOperator & Inverse operator. Returns: std::pair< Eigen::VectorXd, Eigen::VectorXd > — Pair of (snr, snrEst), one value per time point.

Provides the five standard aggregation modes used in MNE-Python's extract_label_time_course(): mean: Simple average across vertices in the label. mean_flip: Mean with sign-flip so that dominant orientation is positive. pca_flip: First PCA component, flipped to align with dominant sign. max: Maximum absolute value at each time point. auto: mean_flip for scalar STCs. src/examples/ex_inv_api/main.cpp const MatrixXd labelMean = InvLabelTimeCourse::extract(stc, {v1}, "mean"); // 1 x 421 const MatrixXd labelMax = InvLabelTimeCourse::extract(stc, {v1}, "max"); // the largest |value| per sample const MatrixXd labelFlip = InvLabelTimeCourse::extract(stc, {v1}, "mean_flip"); // signs flipped by the patch normals

Compute sign-flip vector for a label based on vertex normals. Understand the method Inverse Methods › Sparse Methods Use the API InvMxne InvTfMxne InvGammaMap Run an example Tour of the inverse libraryStart here class mne::InvMxne Mixed-Norm Estimate (MxNE) sparse inverse solver. Minimizes: 0.5 * ||M - G*X||^2_F + alpha * sum_i ||X_i||_2, the objective of mne.inverse_sparse.mixed_norm (without debiasing) using an Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS) approach for the L21-norm (group lasso). MxNE sparse inverse solver. src/examples/ex_inv_api/main.cpp // Whitened data and a gain per nAm make the noise level 1, as mne.inverse_sparse.mixed_norm does. const auto [whitener, rank] = compute_whitener(inverse.noise_cov); // rank 360: 364 channels minus 4 projectors const MNEForwardSolution fixedFwd = MNEForwardSolution(fwdPath, {.force_fixed = true, .surf_ori = true}).pick_regions({v1}).pick_channels(inverse.noise_cov.names); const MatrixXd gain = whitener * fixedFwd.sol.data * 1e-9; const MatrixXd measured = whitener * evoked.pick_channels(inverse.noise_cov.names).data.middleCols(170, 40); // 83-148 ms const double alphaMax = (gain.transpose() * measured).rowwise().norm().maxCoeff(); const InvMxneResult mxne = InvMxne::compute(gain, measured, 0.5 * alphaMax, 1000, 1e-10);

Understand the method Inverse Methods › RAP MUSIC Use the API InvRapMusic InvPwlRapMusic InvTrapMusic Run an example Localize dipoles with RAP-MUSICStart here Localize dipoles with Powell RAP-MUSIC LCMV and DICS beamformers and RAP-MUSIC scanners RAP-MUSIC on raw data with a clustered forward model class mne::InvRapMusic RAP MUSIC (Recursively Applied and Projected Multiple Signal Classification) source localization algorithm. Implements the RAP MUSIC scanning algorithm which iteratively identifies correlated source pairs by projecting the signal subspace and re-scanning the lead field. Each iteration finds one dipole (or dipole pair), projects it out of the signal subspace, and repeats until the desired number of sources is found or the residual correlation drops below threshold. Reference: Mosher & Leahy, IEEE Trans. The resolution matrix R = K · L, where K is the inverse operator (kernel) and L is the lead field (forward operator). Columns of R are point-spread functions (PSFs) and rows are cross-talk functions (CTFs). src/examples/ex_inv_api/main.cpp InvMinimumNorm mne(inverse, lambda2, "MNE"); mne.doInverseSetup(evoked.nave); const MatrixXd& kernel = mne.getKernel(); // 210 source components x 364 good channels const MNEForwardSolution goodFwd = fwd.pick_channels(inverse.noise_cov.names); const MatrixXd resolution = InvResolutionMatrix::compute(kernel, goodFwd.sol.data);

Compute spatial spread (peak-width) metric for each source. The spatial deviation "sd_ext" of mne.minimum_norm.resolution_metrics: the root-mean-square distance from the true source, weighted by the squared PSF. Pass the transposed resolution matrix for the CTF metric. Distances are in the units of matPositions (mne reports cm). Parameters: matResolution : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Resolution matrix (n_sources × n_sources). matPositions : const Eigen::MatrixX3d & Source positions (n_sources × 3). Returns: Eigen::VectorXd — Spatial spread per source (n_sources).

Compute peak localisation error for each source. Distance between true source location and the location of the maximum of the PSF ("peak_err" of mne.minimum_norm.resolution_metrics; pass the transposed resolution matrix for the CTF metric). Parameters: matResolution : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Resolution matrix (n_sources × n_sources). matPositions : const Eigen::MatrixX3d & Source positions (n_sources × 3). Returns: Eigen::VectorXd — Peak localisation error per source (n_sources).

Understand the method Inverse Methods › Sparse Methods Use the API InvMxne InvTfMxne InvGammaMap Run an example Tour of the inverse libraryStart here class mne::InvTfMxne Time-Frequency Mixed-Norm Estimate (TF-MxNE) sparse inverse solver. Solves the inverse problem in the time-frequency domain: min 0.5 * ||M - GZPhi||^2_F + alpha_space * ||Z||_21 + alpha_time * ||Z||_1 where Phi is a Gabor dictionary and Z are the TF coefficients, solved by FISTA. The L21 penalty enforces spatial sparsity (few active sources) while L1 enforces temporal sparsity (focal activations in time-frequency). src/examples/ex_inv_api/main.cpp // TF-MxNE: sparse in space and in a Gabor time-frequency dictionary; 40 samples at 150 Hz. Extends RAP-MUSIC by adding a truncation step to the signal subspace at each iteration, improving robustness to correlated sources. Returns the condition number of a given matrix. Parameters: A : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Matrix to compute the condition number from. s : Eigen::VectorXd & Singular values of A. Returns: double — the condition number.

Find the intersection of two vectors. Parameters: v1 : const Eigen::VectorXi & Input vector 1. v2 : const Eigen::VectorXi & Input vector 2. idx_sel : Eigen::VectorXi & Index of intersection based on v1. Returns: Eigen::VectorXi — the sorted, unique values that are in both of the input arrays.

Make a sparse block diagonal matrix. Returns a sparse block diagonal, diagonalized from the elements in "A". "A" is ma x na, comprising bdn=(na/"n") blocks of submatrices. Each submatrix is ma x "n", and these submatrices are placed down the diagonal of the matrix. Parameters: A : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Matrix which should be diagonalized. n : std::int32_t Columns of the submatrices. Returns: Eigen::SparseMatrix< double > — A sparse block diagonal, diagonalized from the elements in "A".

Creates the pseudo inverse of a matrix. Parameters: a : const Eigen::Matrix< T, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic > & Matrix to compute the pseudo inverse of. Returns: Eigen::Matrix< T, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic > — the pseudo inverse of a.

Returns the rank of a matrix A. Parameters: A : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Matrix to get the rank from. tol : double Relative threshold: biggest singular value multiplied with tol is smallest singular value considered non-zero. Returns: std::int32_t — rank of matrix A.

Thin singular value decomposition that uses all cores for strongly rectangular matrices, such as whitened lead fields with a few hundred channels and tens of thousands of sources. The long dimension is split into blocks that are QR-factorised in parallel (tall-skinny QR); the stacked triangular factors are reduced by a second QR, whose small square factor goes to a divide-and-conquer SVD. Every step is Householder based, so the result is as accurate as a direct divide-and-conquer SVD; only the signs of singular vector pairs may differ. Nearly square or small matrices use the direct SVD. The number of blocks does not depend on the number of cores, so every machine computes the same result. Parameters: A : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Matrix to decompose. Returns: ThinSvd — The singular values and vectors.

Matrix product A * B computed on all cores, by splitting B into a fixed number of column blocks, so the result does not depend on the number of cores. Parameters: A : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Left factor. B : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Right factor; A.cols() must equal B.rows(). Returns: Eigen::MatrixXd — The product A * B.

Sorts a vector (ascending order) in place and returns the track of the original indices. Parameters: v : Eigen::Matrix< T, Eigen::Dynamic, 1 > & Vector to sort; it's sorted in place. desc : bool If true its sorted in a descending order, otherwise ascending (default = true). Returns: Eigen::VectorXi — Vector of the original indices in the new order.

Sorts a vector and a corresponding matrix in place and returns the track of the original indices. The matrix is sorted along the columns using the vector values for comparison. Parameters: v_prime : Eigen::Matrix< T, Eigen::Dynamic, 1 > & Vector to sort (sorted in place). mat : Eigen::Matrix< T, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic > & Matrix to sort (sorted in place). desc : bool If true its sorted in a descending order, otherwise ascending (default = true). Returns: Eigen::VectorXi — Vector of the original indices in the new order.

Compares triplet first entry (row). Parameters: lhs : const Eigen::Triplet< T > & Left triplet. rhs : const Eigen::Triplet< T > & Right triplet. Returns: bool — True if the row index of lhs is less than that of rhs.

Python equivalent scipy.io.savemat in MNE-Python. #include <mne/math/mat_file.h> SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause Copyright (c) 2026 MNE-CPP Authors. mne::write_mat_file stores named matrices uncompressed, in the layout MATLAB's load and SciPy's scipy.io.loadmat read. It is what mne_raw2mat and mne_epochs2mat write. src/examples/ex_math/main.cpp // MATLAB Level 5 MAT-file: load('ex_math.mat') in MATLAB or scipy.io.loadmat in Python const std::filesystem::path matPath = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "ex_math.mat"; MatrixXd sfreq(1, 1); sfreq(0, 0) = 600.0; const auto written = mne::write_mat_file(matPath, "ex_math", {{"data", matrix}, {"sfreq", sfreq}});

Namespace: mne · Library: Math Library Module This page documents a header-level module — a collection of free functions that share an algorithmic topic. There is no enclosing C++ class; the functions live directly in the library namespace. Python equivalent numpy.savetxt / numpy.loadtxt in MNE-Python. #include <mne/math/matrix_io.h> SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause Copyright (c) 2013-2026 MNE-CPP Authors. mne::write_matrix and mne::read_matrix round-trip any dense Eigen expression through plain text, one row per line, so intermediate results can be compared with NumPy (numpy.loadtxt and numpy.savetxt read and write the same layout) and reference data can be checked into a test-data repository. Values are written with enough digits to read back bit-identical; lines containing # are comments. src/examples/ex_math/main.cpp // Plain text, one row per line: numpy.loadtxt reads it, and values read back bit-identical const std::filesystem::path matrixPath = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / "ex_math_matrix.txt"; MatrixXd matrix(2, 3); matrix << 0.1, -2.0 / 3.0, 3.25, 0.0, 1e-6, 42.0; mne::write_matrix(matrix, matrixPath, "example matrix"); MatrixXd readBack; mne::read_matrix(readBack, matrixPath);

bool write_matrix(const Eigen::DenseBase< Derived > & matrix, const std::filesystem::path & path, std::string_view description); Writes a dense matrix as whitespace-separated text, one row per line. Parameters: matrix : const Eigen::DenseBase< Derived > & Matrix, vector or any dense Eigen expression to write. path : const std::filesystem::path & Output file; an existing file is overwritten. description : std::string_view If not empty, a comment header with the dimensions and this description is written first. Returns: bool — True on success, false if the file could not be written.

bool read_matrix(Eigen::Matrix< Scalar, Rows, Cols, Options, MaxRows, MaxCols > & out, const std::filesystem::path & path); Reads a matrix written by write_matrix (or numpy.savetxt). Lines containing # and blank lines are skipped. A row-vector target receives the first row of the file, a column-vector target the first column. Parameters: out : Eigen::Matrix< Scalar, Rows, Cols, Options, MaxRows, MaxCols > & Resized and filled with the values read; left unchanged on failure. path : const std::filesystem::path & Whitespace-separated text file. Returns: bool — True on success, false if the file cannot be opened, holds a non-numeric value, has rows of unequal length or does not fit a fixed-size out.

bool read_matrix(Eigen::Matrix< Scalar, Rows, Cols, Options, MaxRows, MaxCols > & out, std::istream & stream); Reads a matrix in the same text layout from a stream, e.g. the captured output of a Python script. Parameters: out : Eigen::Matrix< Scalar, Rows, Cols, Options, MaxRows, MaxCols > & Resized and filled with the values read; left unchanged on failure. stream : std::istream & Whitespace-separated text, one row per line. Returns: bool — True on success, false if the text holds a non-numeric value, has rows of unequal length or does not fit a fixed-size out.
bool parse_matrix(Eigen::Matrix< Scalar, Rows, Cols, Options, MaxRows, MaxCols > & out, std::istream & file, std::string_view source);

Namespace: mne · Library: Math Library · Source: math/simplex_algorithm.h Python equivalent scipy.optimize.fmin in MNE-Python. #include <mne/math/simplex_algorithm.h> class mne::SimplexAlgorithm Header-only Nelder–Mead simplex minimiser templated on the scalar type and on the cost / report callables, implementing the Strategy pattern at zero runtime cost (the functors are inlined by the compiler). Header-only Nelder–Mead simplex minimiser with templated cost and report functors. src/examples/ex_math/main.cpp // Minimise the Rosenbrock function from a 3-vertex simplex around (-1, 1); ftol is relative, so the // minimum value is offset to 1 (a minimum of exactly 0 never satisfies a relative tolerance) auto rosenbrock = [](const VectorXd& x) { return 1.0 + 100.0 * std::pow(x(1) - x(0) * x(0), 2) + std::pow(1.0 - x(0), 2); }; MatrixXd simplex(3, 2); simplex << -1.0, 1.0, -0.9, 1.0, -1.0, 1.1; VectorXd values(3); for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) { values(i) = rosenbrock(simplex.row(i).transpose()); } int evaluations = 0; const bool converged = SimplexAlgorithm::simplex_minimize<double>(simplex, values, 1e-12, 0.0, rosenbrock, 5000, evaluations); Index best = 0; values.minCoeff(&best); // vertices are not sorted on return

Namespace: mne · Source: src/libs/mne/ml The mne_ml library (mne_ml namespace) provides machine learning infrastructure for MNE-CPP: ONNX Runtime inference for pre-trained neural networks, tensor data structures, and a launcher for Python training scripts. Classical estimators live in the libraries that use them, such as the covariance shrinkage in mne_sts and the Local Outlier Factor in mne_dsp. The primary use case is CMNE (Contextual Minimum-Norm Estimate) inference, where an LSTM network trained in Python is deployed via ONNX Runtime in C++. target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE mne_ml) Dependencies: mne_base, mne_math, mne_pybridge (except on WebAssembly), Qt6::Core, Eigen3. Optional: ONNX Runtime (enabled via USE_ONNXRUNTIME=ON).

Namespace: mne · Library: Machine Learning Library · Source: ml/ml_tensor.h #include <mne/ml/ml_tensor.h> class mne::MlTensor N-dimensional row-major float32 tensor with shared-buffer storage, Eigen Map accessors and a non-owning view mode. The shape is an arbitrary std::vector<int64_t> (matching ONNX Runtime), the buffer is a reference-counted std::vector<float> (or external memory in view mode), and copy / reshape / slice all stay O(1) by sharing the underlying storage. Namespace: mne · Source: src/libs/mne/mne The Mne library contains the core neuroscience data structures used throughout MNE-CPP — source spaces, source estimates, forward solutions, inverse operators, hemispheres, BEM surfaces, covariance matrices, epochs, projections, and many supporting geometry types. It is the C++ counterpart of the structures defined in the original MNE-C libmne and the core mne Python package. All classes reside in the mne_mne namespace.
The library mirrors the data model of the original MNE software closely. Most classes are direct C++ translations of the MNE-C structs with added Qt/Eigen integration.

Reads MNE-C's text syntax (mne_make_derivations in). Each derivation is name = followed by terms joined by + and -; a term is a channel name optionally preceded by a weight and *, e.g. "EEG 001-EEG 002" = "EEG 001" - "EEG 002". Names with spaces are quoted, tokens are separated by white space and # starts a comment line. Weights of the same input channel add up; derivations whose weights are all zero are dropped. Parameters: path : const std::filesystem::path & The text file. Returns: std::optional< MNEDerivSet > — One derivation holding all definitions, or no value on a syntax error.

Reads an MNE-C text event file (MNE-C mne_load_events). Each line holds sample, time, trigger value before and after, and an optional comment; # starts a comment line. A negative sample is computed from the time. A first line with both trigger values 0 marks the current format: it gives the first sample of the recording and is not an event. Old files have no such line; their samples are shifted by old_offset instead. Namespace: mne · Library: MNE Library Module This page documents a header-level module — a collection of free functions that share an algorithmic topic. There is no enclosing C++ class; the functions live directly in the library namespace. Python equivalent mne.coreg.Coregistration in MNE-Python. #include <mne/mne/mne_icp.h> SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause Copyright (c) 2020-2026 MNE-CPP Authors. Free functions for the point-to-surface ICP used by mne-cpp's coregistration tools to refine an initial head <-> MRI transformation: mne::fitMatchedPoints aligns matched point pairs (e.g. fiducials), mne::discard3DPointOutliers drops points far from the surface, and mne::performIcp projects each point onto the nearest triangle of an MNEBemSurface (via MNEProjectToSurface), solves a rigid-body least squares with SVD and iterates until convergence. src/examples/ex_mne_api/main.cpp // 1. Rough start from three matched points (e.g. the fiducials) Matrix4f start; MatrixXf mriPoints(3, 3); mriPoints << innerSkull.rr.row(0), innerSkull.rr.row(20), innerSkull.rr.row(40); fitMatchedPoints(headShape.topRows(3), mriPoints, start); FiffCoordTrans headToMri(FIFFV_COORD_HEAD, FIFFV_COORD_MRI, start); // 2. Drop head shape points further than 10 mm from the surface, then refine with ICP auto surface = std::make_shared<MNEProjectToSurface>(innerSkull); VectorXi take; MatrixXf kept; discard3DPointOutliers(surface, headShape, headToMri, take, kept, 0.01f); float rmse = 0.0f; performIcp(surface, kept, headToMri, rmse, false, 50, 1e-6f);

documents.t: Assemble the inverse kernel matrix. Applies eigenfield/eigenlead decomposition, regularisation, whitening, projection, and optional noise normalisation to produce the kernel matrix that maps sensor data to source estimates. Parameters: label : const FsLabel & Cortical label restricting the source space (empty for all sources). method : const std::string & Inverse method: "MNE", "dSPM", or "sLORETA". pick_normal : bool If true, keep only the surface-normal component (requires free orientation). K : Eigen::MatrixXd & Assembled kernel matrix (nSources x nChannels). noise_norm : Eigen::SparseMatrix< double > & Diagonal noise-normalisation matrix (empty for MNE). vertno : std::vector< Eigen::VectorXi > & Vertex numbers per hemisphere. Returns: bool — true on success.

Cluster the inverse kernel by cortical parcellation. Groups source-space points within each parcellation label using KMeans and returns a reduced kernel together with the cluster operator. Parameters: annotationSet : const FsAnnotationSet & Annotation set for left and right hemisphere. clusterSize : std::int32_t Maximum number of sources per cluster. D : Eigen::MatrixXd & Cluster operator matrix (nSources x nClusters). method : const std::string & Distance metric: "cityblock" or "sqeuclidean". Returns: Eigen::MatrixXd — Clustered kernel matrix.
Access the most recently assembled kernel (mutable). Returns: Eigen::MatrixXd & — Reference to the kernel matrix.
Access the most recently assembled kernel (const). Returns: Eigen::MatrixXd — Copy of the kernel matrix.
Check whether the inverse operator uses fixed source orientations. Returns: bool — true if orientation is fixed-normal.

Prepare the inverse operator for source estimation. Scales covariances by the number of averages, builds the regularised pseudo-inverse, the whitener, the SSP projector, and (optionally) the noise-normalisation factors for dSPM or sLORETA. Parameters: nave : std::int32_t Number of averages (scales the noise covariance). lambda2 : float Regularisation parameter (SNR^{-2}). dSPM : bool Compute dSPM noise-normalisation factors. sLORETA : bool Compute sLORETA noise-normalisation factors. Returns: MNEInverseOperator — A prepared copy of the inverse operator ready for apply_inverse.

Writes the inverse solution block into an open FIFF stream. Parameters: stream : FiffStream & Open FIFF stream.

Assemble an inverse operator from a forward solution and noise covariance. Performs depth weighting, source-covariance construction, whitening, and SVD decomposition of the weighted lead-field matrix. Parameters: info : const FiffInfo & Measurement info; bad channels in info.bads are excluded. forward : MNEForwardSolution Forward operator (modified internally for fixed orientation if needed). noiseCov : const FiffCov & Noise covariance matrix. loose : float Tangential-component weight in [0, 1]. depth : float Depth-weighting exponent in [0, 1]; 0 disables. fixed : bool Use fixed surface-normal orientations. limit_depth_chs : bool Restrict depth weighting to gradiometers (or fallback). Returns: MNEInverseOperator — Assembled inverse operator.

Namespace: mne · Library: MNE Library · Source: mne/mne_layout_port.h #include <mne/mne/mne_layout_port.h> class mne::MNELayoutPort Single viewport of a plotter layout (one line of an MNE-C .lout file). Channel names are stored in matching form: lower case, without spaces and without anything after a dash (MNE-C mne_lout_clean_name), so "MEG 0113" and "meg0113" select the same port and a CTF "MLC11-2622" matches "MLC11". src/examples/ex_mne_api/main.cpp // The Neuromag Vectorview layout: one viewport per channel auto layout = MNELayout::read((layoutDir + "/Vectorview-all.lout").toStdU16String()); const std::map<std::string, Eigen::Vector2d> positions = layout->channelPositions(); // lower-left corners, keyed "MEG 0113" const int leftHalf = layout->confine(Eigen::AlignedBox2d(Eigen::Vector2d(-85.0, -83.0), Eigen::Vector2d(0.0, 75.0))); // zoom to the left half const int shownTriplet = layout->matchPorts({"MEG 0113", "MEG 0112", "MEG 0111"});

Projects the whitened data on the eigenfields (MNE-C mne_project_to_eigen_fields) and estimates SNR and lambda2_est per time point (MNE-C compute_regularization, noise method). SNR is the power of the whitened data per non-zero noise eigenvalue (the square of mne.minimum_norm.estimate_snr's snr). lambda2_est is 100 where SNR < 1; elsewhere it starts at 10 and shrinks by 0.9 until the squared prediction error of the whitened data falls below the chi^2 point at p = 0.001 with one degree of freedom less than the components used. Parameters: inv : const MNEInverseOperator & A prepared inverse operator. data : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Measured data, one row per channel of inv, one column per time.

Selects lambda2 per time point (MNE-C select_regularization): trace_ratio / snr for a positive power SNR, lambda2_est otherwise. trace_ratio is the mean squared singular value. Parameters: inv : const MNEInverseOperator & The prepared inverse operator used for computeRegularization. snr : double Power SNR, <= 0 to use lambda2_est.

Computes the data the minimum-norm estimate predicts with the selected lambda2, colored back to the sensors (MNE-C compute_predicted_data; the data part of mne.minimum_norm.apply_inverse's residual). Parameters: inv : const MNEInverseOperator & The prepared inverse operator used for computeRegularization.

Fills all fields for one data set: projects it on the eigenfields, estimates the SNR and lambda2 per time point, selects the lambda2 to use and computes the predicted data. Parameters: inv : const MNEInverseOperator & An inverse operator prepared with MNEInverseOperator::prepare_inverse_operator. data : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Measured data, one row per channel of inv in its order, one column per time. snr : double Power SNR for a fixed lambda2 (see selectRegularization), <= 0 to use lambda2_est. Returns: MNEMneData — The MNE data.

Computes the map between two registered spheres (MNE-C mne_compose_morph_maps, accurate mode; mne.surface._make_morph_map_hemi). Both spheres are scaled to unit radius. Namespace: mne · Library: MNE Library · Source: mne/mne_named_matrix.h #include <mne/mne/mne_named_matrix.h> class mne::MNENamedMatrix A dense matrix with named rows and columns. MNENamedMatrix associates a dense float matrix (Eigen::MatrixXf) with optional row and column name lists (StringList). It is the C++ equivalent of the MNE-C mneNamedMatrixRec struct, and is used throughout the library to represent projection vectors, CTF compensation matrices, and forward-solution gain matrices. The class provides factory methods to: build() a matrix from its constituent parts, read() a matrix from a FIFF stream, and pick() a sub-matrix by selecting named rows and/or columns. All factory methods return std::unique_ptr<MNENamedMatrix> for clear ownership. src/examples/ex_mne_api/main.cpp // Open a third-order gradiometer recording and read it uncompensated (grade 0) std::unique_ptr<MNERawData> ctfRaw(MNERawData::open_file_comp(ctfPath.toStdU16String(), false, false, MNEFilterDef(), 0)); const MNECTFCompDataSet& comp = *ctfRaw->comp; // grades 1, 2, 3 and two 4D kinds const MNECTFCompData* third = nullptr; for (const auto& c : comp.comps) { if (c->kind == MNECTFCompDataSet::map_comp_kind(3)) { third = c.get(); } } const int grade = MNECTFCompDataSet::get_comp(ctfRaw->info->chInfo, ctfRaw->info->nchan); MNERawData::RowMajorMatrixXf ctf(ctfRaw->info->nchan, 21); ctfRaw->pick_data(nullptr, ctfRaw->first_samp, ctf);

Patch information for a single source space point including vertex members and area.
Constructs the MNE Patch Information Refactored: mne_new_patch (mne_source_space.c).
Destroys the MNE Patch Information Refactored: mne_free_patch (mne_source_space.c).

Calculates the total surface area of this patch. Iterates over all member vertices of the patch. For each vertex, sums one-third of the area of every neighboring triangle. The factor of 1/3 accounts for each triangle being shared among its three vertices. The result is stored in the member variable area. Refactored from: calculate_patch_area (mne_patches.c). Parameters: s : *MNESourceSpace ** Pointer to the source space containing the triangle mesh (neighbor triangles and triangle areas).

Calculates the average surface normal and its deviation for this patch. Computes the mean normal direction (ave_nn) by summing the normals of all member vertices and normalizing the result to unit length. Then computes the average angular deviation (dev_nn) of each member vertex normal from the mean normal, in radians, using the arccosine of the dot product. Parameters: s : *MNESourceSpace ** Pointer to the source space containing vertex normals (nn) for each vertex in the mesh.

Namespace: mne · Library: MNE Library · Source: mne/mne_raw_buf_def.h #include <mne/mne/mne_raw_buf_def.h> class mne::MNERawBufDef Definition of one raw data buffer within a FIFF file. Each MNERawBufDef describes a contiguous chunk of samples, either loaded from the FIFF file or produced by the overlap-add filter pipeline. Sample values are stored in a row-major matrix (nchan x ns) that is managed by an external ring buffer; an empty (0x0) matrix indicates that the data are not currently resident in memory. src/examples/ex_mne_api/main.cpp // MNE-C style reader: buffer directory, channel selection, projection and overlap-add filter MNEFilterDef filter; // 40 Hz lowpass, 5 Hz transition, 4096-sample blocks filter.filter_on = true; filter.size = 4096; filter.taper_size = 2048; filter.lowpass = filter.eog_lowpass = 40.0f; filter.lowpass_width = filter.eog_lowpass_width = 5.0f; std::unique_ptr<MNERawData> mneRaw(MNERawData::open_file(rawFile.fileName().toStdU16String(), false, false, filter)); const MNERawInfo& rawInfo = *mneRaw->info; const MNERawBufDef& firstBuffer = mneRaw->bufs.front(); MNEChSelection sel; // channel names are stored without spaces sel.chspick = sel.chspick_nospace = {"MEG 0113", "EEG 001", "EOG 061"}; sel.pick_deriv = VectorXi::Constant(sel.nchan(), -1); sel.pick.resize(sel.nchan()); for (int c = 0; c < sel.nchan(); ++c) { sel.pick[c] = static_cast<int>(mne::index_of(mneRaw->ch_names, sel.chspick[c])); } const int ns = 25; MNERawData::RowMajorMatrixXf segment(sel.nchan(), ns); mneRaw->pick_data(&sel, mneRaw->first_samp + 2990, segment); // calibrated, across a buffer boundary const double eegRaw = segment(1, 0); mneRaw->pick_data_filt(&sel, mneRaw->first_samp + 2990, segment); const double eegFilt = segment(1, 0); // The file stores its 4 SSP projectors as inactive; make_projection switches them on std::unique_ptr<MNEProjOp> proj = MNEProjOp::make_projection({rawFile.fileName().toStdU16String()}, rawInfo.chInfo).value(); proj->assign_channels(mneRaw->ch_names); const bool compiled = proj->make_proj(); const MNEProjItem& firstItem = proj->items[0]; mneRaw->proj = std::move(proj); mneRaw->pick_data_proj(&sel, mneRaw->first_samp + 2990, segment); const double eegProj = segment(1, 0);

Finds the nearest FIFFB_MEAS parent node in the FIFF directory tree. Walks up the tree from the given node by following parent pointers until a node of type FIFFB_MEAS is found. Returns: std::shared_ptr< FiffDirNode > — Shared pointer to the enclosing FIFFB_MEAS node, or an empty shared pointer if no such node is found.

Finds the FIFFB_MEAS_INFO child node within the nearest FIFFB_MEAS block. Parameters: node : const std::shared_ptr< FiffDirNode > & Starting node from which to search. Returns: std::shared_ptr< FiffDirNode > — Shared pointer to the FIFFB_MEAS_INFO node, or an empty shared pointer if not found.

Finds the raw data block in the FIFF directory tree. Searches the tree under the given node for a FIFFB_RAW_DATA block. If none is found, falls back to searching for a FIFFB_CONTINUOUS_DATA block. Returns: std::shared_ptr< FiffDirNode > — Shared pointer to the raw data directory node, or an empty shared pointer if neither raw nor continuous data blocks are found.

Finds the MaxShield raw data block in the FIFF directory tree. Searches the tree under the given node for a FIFFB_SMSH_RAW_DATA block, which contains SSS/MaxShield processed raw data. Namespace: mne · Library: MRI Library · Source: mri/mri_vol_data.h #include <mne/mri/mri_vol_data.h> class mne::MriVolData Format-agnostic 3D MRI volume: header geometry, voxel buffer (as a vector of MriSlice), scan parameters and provenance. The volume is the single in-memory representation every consumer in mne-cpp operates on, regardless of whether it was loaded from MGH/MGZ, NIfTI-1 or a FreeSurfer COR directory. Storage is decomposed into a vector of MriSlice so the COR.fif writer can serialise without an intermediate copy, while the slice viewer and the BEM coregistration step both index it through the same (column, row, slice) coordinate. The header captures FreeSurfer's MGH conventions: voxel sizes (spacingX/Y/Z), direction cosines (Mdc, column-major), centre RAS (c_ras) and voxel data type (MRI_UCHAR / MRI_INT / MRI_FLOAT / MRI_SHORT). Optional scan parameters (TR, flip angle, TE, TI, FoV) and tags (Talairach transform path, provenance) round out the structure. The read() entry point dispatches on the file extension so callers do not need to branch on format. Format reference: https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/fswiki/FsTutorial/MghFormat Ported from mneMRIdataRec in MNE C (mne_types_mne-c.h) by Matti Hamalainen. src/examples/ex_mri/main.cpp MriVolData nifti; nifti.read((dataDir + "/gradient.nii.gz").toStdString()); // the suffix selects the NIfTI reader

Namespace: mne · Source: src/libs/mne/sts The mne_sts library (mne_sts namespace) provides statistical testing and evaluation tools for MEG/EEG analysis: parametric tests (t-tests, F-tests), non-parametric cluster permutation testing, multiple comparison correction, covariance estimation with shrinkage methods, spatial adjacency construction, and source-level evaluation metrics. target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE mne_sts) Dependencies: mne_base, mne_math, mne_fiff, Qt6::Core, Eigen3.

Returns std::pair<Eigen::MatrixXd, double> (covariance matrix, shrinkage coefficient α∈[0,1]\alpha \in [0,1]α∈[0,1]). The Ledoit-Wolf estimator computes the optimal linear shrinkage coefficient analytically using the formula from Ledoit & Wolf (2004), producing a well-conditioned covariance matrix even when the number of variables exceeds the number of observations.

Build a spatial adjacency matrix from a triangulated source space. Build a spatio-temporal adjacency matrix from a triangulated source space. Constructs a (nVerticesnTimes) x (nVerticesnTimes) adjacency matrix where spatial neighbors come from the triangle mesh and temporal neighbors connect each vertex to itself at t-1 and t+1. The linear index is vertex * nTimes + time. Parameters: tris : const Eigen::MatrixX3i & Triangle definitions (nTris x 3, vertex indices). nVertices : int Total number of vertices. nTimes : int Number of time points. Returns: Eigen::SparseMatrix< int > — Sparse adjacency matrix (symmetric, nVerticesnTimes x nVerticesnTimes).

Adjacency of a regular 1-D grid of n points (each linked to its two neighbours), the meaning of an integer dimension in mne.stats.combine_adjacency. Parameters: n : int Number of points. Returns: Eigen::SparseMatrix< int > — Sparse adjacency matrix (n x n), no diagonal.

Combine the adjacency of several dimensions, as mne.stats.combine_adjacency: points are flattened in C order (the last dimension varies fastest), two points are adjacent when they differ in one dimension and are adjacent there, and every point is adjacent to itself. Parameters: dims : const std::vector< Eigen::SparseMatrix< int > > & Square 0/1 adjacency per dimension (diagonals are ignored). Returns: Eigen::SparseMatrix< int > — Sparse adjacency matrix over the product of the dimensions.

Each matrix is nVertices x nTimes. adjacency : const Eigen::SparseMatrix< int > & Spatio-temporal adjacency matrix (nVerticesnTimes x nVerticesnTimes). threshold : double Cluster-forming t-threshold. nPermutations : int Number of sign-flip permutations. tail : StatsTailType Tail type for the test. F-test cluster-based permutation test for one-way ANOVA. Tests for differences across conditions by randomly reassigning condition labels and computing max cluster F-statistics. Parameters: conditions : const std::vector< std::vector< Eigen::MatrixXd > > & Vector of conditions, each containing per-subject matrices (nVertices x nTimes). adjacency : const Eigen::SparseMatrix< int > & Spatio-temporal adjacency matrix (nVerticesnTimes x nVerticesnTimes). threshold : double Cluster-forming F-threshold. nPermutations : int Number of permutations. Returns: StatsClusterResult — StatsClusterResult with observed F-map (in matTObs), cluster statistics, and p-values.

Threshold-Free Cluster Enhancement (TFCE). Enhances a statistic map by integrating cluster extent and height over a range of thresholds (Smith & Nichols 2009). Handles both positive and negative values. Both signs are swept by the thresholds h = k * dh, k = 1..nSteps, with dh = max|statMap| / (nSteps + 1), like MNE-Python's threshold=dict(start=dh, step=dh). Parameters: statMap : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Statistic map (nVertices x nTimes). adjacency : const Eigen::SparseMatrix< int > & Spatio-temporal adjacency matrix (nVerticesnTimes x nVerticesnTimes). E : double Extent exponent (default 0.5). H : double Height exponent (default 2.0). nSteps : int Number of threshold steps (default 100). Returns: Eigen::MatrixXd — TFCE-enhanced score map (nVertices x nTimes).

Ledoit-Wolf optimal shrinkage covariance estimator. Computes the shrinkage coefficient analytically using the formula from Ledoit & Wolf (2004) "A well-conditioned estimator for large-dimensional covariance matrices" (Journal of Multivariate Analysis, 88(2), 365-411). Parameters: matData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Zero-mean data, n_channels x n_samples. Returns: std::pair< Eigen::MatrixXd, double > — std::pair containing the shrunk covariance matrix (n_channels x n_channels) and the shrinkage coefficient alpha in [0,1].

Oracle Approximating Shrinkage (OAS) covariance estimator. Implements the OAS formula from Chen, Wiesel, Eldar & Hero (2010) "Shrinkage Algorithms for MMSE Covariance Estimation" (IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 58(10), 5016-5029). Parameters: matData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Zero-mean data, n_channels x n_samples. Returns: std::pair< Eigen::MatrixXd, double > — std::pair containing the shrunk covariance matrix and the shrinkage coefficient rho in [0,1].

Fixed diagonal regularisation. Computes the sample covariance and adds a fixed fraction of the mean eigenvalue to the diagonal: C_reg = C + reg * trace(C)/p * I. Parameters: matData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Zero-mean data, n_channels x n_samples. dReg : double Regularisation fraction (default 0.1). Returns: std::pair< Eigen::MatrixXd, double > — std::pair containing the regularised covariance and dReg.

PCA-based rank-reduced covariance estimator. Computes covariance in the subspace of the top-k principal components. Components beyond rank are zeroed. If iRank <= 0, the rank is estimated from the eigenvalue spectrum. Parameters: matData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Zero-mean data, n_channels x n_samples. iRank : int Number of principal components to retain (0 = auto). Returns: std::pair< Eigen::MatrixXd, double > — std::pair containing the rank-reduced covariance and the effective rank used.

Factor Analysis covariance estimator via EM algorithm. Decomposes covariance as C = W*W^T + Psi, where W is a low-rank loading matrix and Psi is a diagonal noise matrix. Uses the EM algorithm from Rubin & Thayer (1982). Parameters: matData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Zero-mean data, n_channels x n_samples. iNFactors : int Number of latent factors (default: min(p,n)/2). iMaxIter : int Maximum EM iterations (default 200). dTol : double Convergence tolerance on log-likelihood (default 1e-6). Returns: std::pair< Eigen::MatrixXd, double > — std::pair containing the Factor Analysis covariance and the final log-likelihood.

Auto-select the best covariance estimator via cross-validation. Runs all available estimators (empirical, shrunk/LW, OAS, diagonal_fixed, PCA, factor_analysis) and selects the one with the highest average Gaussian log-likelihood on held-out folds. Parameters: matData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Zero-mean data, n_channels x n_samples. iNFolds : int Number of cross-validation folds (default 3). Returns: std::pair< Eigen::MatrixXd, double > — std::pair containing the best covariance matrix and the index of the winning method (0=empirical, 1=shrunk, 2=oas, 3=diagonal_fixed, 4=pca, 5=factor_analysis).

Gaussian log-likelihood of held-out data given a covariance model. Computes: -0.5 * (p * log(2π) + log|Σ| + trace(Σ^{-1} * S_test)) where S_test is the sample covariance of the test data. Parameters: matTestData : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Zero-mean test data, n_channels x n_test_samples. matCov : const Eigen::MatrixXd & Covariance model, n_channels x n_channels. Returns: double — Average log-likelihood per sample.
