Namespace: mne::viz::qt · Source: src/libs/mne/viz/backends/qt mne_viz_qt (namespace mne::viz::qt, src/libs/mne/viz/backends/qt) is the Qt backend of mne_viz. mne_viz describes what a viewer shows and how it behaves without a GUI toolkit; this library renders and hosts it with Qt: Folder Contents plots/ 2-D plots and the QRhi renderer of mne::viz GPU frames (RhiFrameRenderer) viewers/ Qt windows, widgets, settings panels built from mne::viz::SettingsForm, and Qt item models adapting the mne::viz view models 3d/ The 3-D brain view described below It is the only library that uses Qt (Qt Gui, which includes QRhi, and Qt Widgets). Further backends of mne_viz go next to it under src/libs/mne/viz/backends/. target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE mne_viz_qt)

Starting with MNE-CPP v2.0, the 3D visualization library has been rebuilt on top of Qt's Rendering Hardware Interface (RHI). It lives in 3d/ of mne_viz_qt (namespace mne::viz::qt). Unlike the previous Qt3D-based implementation, the RHI backend talks directly to the platform's native graphics API — Metal on macOS, Vulkan on Linux, Direct3D 11/12 on Windows, or OpenGL as a fallback — giving MNE-CPP a thinner, more portable rendering stack. Why RHI? Qt3D provided a high-level scene-graph but added significant abstraction overhead. With RHI, the library manages its own render pipeline, vertex buffers, and shader programs directly, resulting in lower latency, smaller binary size, and better control over GPU resource lifetime — all critical for real-time neuroimaging visualization.

The library follows a clean separation of concerns inspired by several well-known software patterns: Model–View separation — The BrainTreeModel (a QStandardItemModel) owns all scene data and metadata. BrainView reads the model to decide what to show; BrainRenderer decides how to draw it. Neither the model nor the renderer know about each other directly — BrainView acts as the mediator. Retained-mode rendering — Renderable objects (BrainSurface, DipoleObject, NetworkObject, SourceEstimateOverlay) each own their GPU resources (vertex buffers, index buffers, instance buffers, uniform buffers). They create these resources once on initialization and only update the data that changes per frame (e.g., vertex colors for a new time sample). This avoids per-frame allocation and keeps draw calls cheap. Strategy pattern for shaders — The BrainRenderer maintains a set of pre-compiled shader pipelines (Standard, Holographic, Anatomical, Dipole, XRay, ShowNormals). Switching visual style is a pipeline swap, not a recompilation. Observer / worker pattern — Real-time data (sensor streams, source estimates) flows through dedicated QObject-based workers running on background threads. Workers emit signals carrying per-vertex color arrays, which BrainView applies to the appropriate renderable before the next draw call. This keeps the render thread free from heavy computation. Composition over inheritance — Rather than deep inheritance hierarchies (as in the old Qt3D design where every renderable was a QEntity subclass), the RHI design composes independent objects: a BrainSurface is not a widget or an entity — it is a plain C++ object that knows how to upload geometry and draw itself when asked. Key Differences from the Qt3D Implementation​ Aspect Qt3D (v1.x) RHI (v2.0) Widget base Custom QWidget + QSurface3DFormat QRhiWidget Render control Qt3D framegraph / scenegraph Direct QRhi pipeline + command buffer Shader language GLSL via Qt3D materials GLSL compiled per-backend by Qt RHI Data model Data3DTreeModel + Renderable3DEntity → QEntity BrainTreeModel + BrainSurface / DipoleObject / NetworkObject Multi-view Not built-in MultiViewLayout with 1–4 panes Instanced rendering GeometryMultiplier Native QRhi instance buffers Vertex picking Not implemented RayPicker with CPU ray–triangle intersection Graphics backends OpenGL only Metal, Vulkan, D3D 11/12, OpenGL

View Layer​ The view layer implements the Mediator pattern — BrainView sits between user input, the data model, and the renderer, coordinating their interactions without letting them reference each other directly. BrainView — The top-level widget, inheriting from QRhiWidget (Qt's portable RHI surface widget). On each frame, Qt calls BrainView::render(), which assembles a SceneData struct containing the current MVP matrix, camera position, light direction, and overlay mode, then hands it to BrainRenderer for drawing. BrainView also handles all mouse/keyboard events and dispatches them to the CameraController (for orbit/zoom/pan) or RayPicker (for vertex selection). It supports two modes: SingleView with an interactive orbiting camera, and MultiView with up to four fixed-angle viewports (e.g., top, left, front, free). MultiViewLayout — A pure-geometry helper with no widget dependencies. It stores fractional split positions and computes viewport rectangles, splitter hit-testing, and minimum pane sizes. BrainView queries this class for the pixel rectangles of each pane before issuing scissored draw calls. The layout supports 1, 2, 3, or 4 panes with draggable separators. Render Engine​ The render engine is where the Strategy pattern is most visible. BrainRenderer holds a map of pre-compiled QRhiGraphicsPipeline objects — one per ShaderMode — and selects the appropriate pipeline at draw time. BrainRenderer — The low-level workhorse. It creates and caches QRhiGraphicsPipeline objects, manages shared uniform buffers (for the scene-wide MVP and lighting data), and iterates over all visible renderables to issue draw calls. Each renderable provides its own vertex/index/instance buffers; BrainRenderer simply binds them and calls drawIndexed() or draw(). The renderer is stateless between frames — all per-frame data arrives via the SceneData struct, making it easy to render the same scene from multiple camera angles (multi-view). GLSL Shaders — One shader program per ShaderMode, plus programs for electrodes, MRI slices and video overlays, each consisting of a .vert and .frag file. Qt's RHI layer compiles these at load time into the native shading language of the active backend (Metal Shading Language, SPIR-V for Vulkan, HLSL for D3D, or GLSL for OpenGL). The shaders receive per-vertex attributes (position, normal, packed ABGR color, packed ABGR annotation color) and a uniform block with the scene data. The overlayMode uniform controls which color channel the fragment shader samples — surface, annotation, scientific colormap, or source estimate. ShaderMode Shader Visual Style Standard standard Phong lighting (default) Holographic holographic Two-sided holographic effect Anatomical anatomical Curvature-based coloring Dipole dipole Dipole cone rendering XRay holographic Semi-transparent x-ray (additive front faces) ShowNormals shownormals Surface-normal visualization Renderable Objects​ Renderables follow the Self-Contained Resource pattern — each object manages the full lifecycle of its GPU resources (creation, update, destruction) and exposes a uniform interface (initResources(), updateResources(), draw()) that BrainRenderer calls. This keeps the renderer agnostic about data types. Class Purpose GPU Resources BrainSurface Cortical or BEM mesh with per-vertex curvature, annotation, and STC color channels Vertex buffer (VertexData: pos, normal, ABGR base, ABGR annotation), index buffer, uniform buffer DipoleObject Equivalent current dipoles rendered as instanced cones pointing in the moment direction Shared cone geometry + per-instance transform/color buffer NetworkObject Connectivity graph — nodes as instanced spheres (diameter ∝ degree), edges as instanced cylinders (diameter and color ∝ weight) Shared sphere/cylinder geometry + per-instance transform/color buffers SourceEstimateOverlay Per-vertex STC amplitude overlay streamed onto a BrainSurface Updates the host surface's vertex color channel in-place The VertexData struct deserves special mention. It packs four attributes into a compact interleaved layout: struct VertexData { QVector3D pos; // vertex position QVector3D norm; // vertex normal uint32_t color; // curvature / base color (ABGR packed) uint32_t colorAnnotation; // annotation region color (ABGR packed) }; Colors are stored as packed uint32_t values (packABGR()) rather than QVector4D floats, halving the per-vertex color footprint — a meaningful saving for high-resolution cortical meshes with 160 000+ vertices. Data Model​ The data model applies the Composite pattern via Qt's QStandardItemModel tree structure. Every scene object is represented as a tree item; parent items group children logically (subject → hemisphere → surface, or subject → measurement → network). The tree can be displayed in a QTreeView to give users interactive visibility toggles, color pickers, and threshold sliders without any custom widget work. Crucially, tree items in the RHI design are not renderables. In the old Qt3D design, Renderable3DEntity was a QEntity — the data model and the scenegraph were one and the same. In the RHI design, tree items are pure data/metadata containers. BrainView reads the model to decide which BrainSurface, DipoleObject, or NetworkObject instances should be visible, then passes them to BrainRenderer. This separation makes it straightforward to render the same data in multiple viewports with different visibility profiles. Tree Item Data Source SurfaceTreeItem FreeSurfer surface + annotation BemTreeItem BEM compartment surface DigitizerTreeItem / DigitizerSetTreeItem HPI, fiducials, head-shape points DipoleTreeItem ECDSet NetworkTreeItem Network from the Connectivity library SourceSpaceTreeItem MNESourceSpace Core​ The core module provides shared types and state that every other module depends on, without pulling in heavy Qt or QRhi headers. RenderTypes — A lightweight header-only file defining ShaderMode and VisualizationMode enums and the packABGR() utility. It deliberately avoids any QRhi includes, so public API headers can use these enums without leaking GPU implementation details to downstream consumers. ViewState — Captures all per-viewport settings: camera orientation, lighting parameters, and a ViewVisibilityProfile struct with independent boolean toggles for each data layer (LH, RH, BEM head, BEM outer skull, BEM inner skull, MEG sensors, etc.). Each viewport in a multi-view layout carries its own ViewState, enabling pane-specific views of the same dataset. DataLoader — Centralized utilities for loading FreeSurfer surfaces, annotations, and BEM data into the model and creating the corresponding renderables. Input​ Input handling is decoupled from the widget, following the Strategy pattern — BrainView delegates input interpretation to specialized objects rather than handling it in monolithic mousePressEvent overrides. CameraController — A widget-independent camera that takes mouse delta values and produces a CameraResult struct (projection, view, and model matrices, plus camera position and up vector). It supports orbiting around a focus point, dolly zoom, and panning. Because it has no widget dependency, it can compute matrices for any viewport rectangle, which is how multi-view rendering works — BrainView calls CameraController once per pane with different viewport sizes. RayPicker — Performs CPU-side ray–triangle intersection testing against all visible BrainSurface meshes. Given a mouse position and viewport rectangle, it unprojects a ray and walks the triangle list of each surface to find the closest intersection. The result is a PickResult carrying the hit point, surface key, vertex index, distance, and (if available) the FreeSurfer annotation region name and label ID. Dipole picking is also supported. Scene Managers​ Scene managers encapsulate domain-specific logic that would otherwise bloat BrainView. Each manager owns the lifecycle of its workers and the mapping between raw data and renderable updates. SensorFieldMapper — Computes and caches the sparse interpolation matrix that maps sensor-level data (MEG channels or EEG electrodes) onto a scalp or helmet surface mesh. When new samples arrive, it multiplies the data vector by the interpolation matrix to produce per-vertex color values. SourceEstimateManager — Handles loading and streaming of MNE source estimates (STC files or real-time data). It manages the interpolation from source-space vertices to the high-resolution cortical surface mesh and drives the SourceEstimateOverlay. RtSensorStreamManager — Lifecycle manager for RtSensorDataController. It encapsulates the start/stop/configure cycle of real-time sensor streaming, keeping BrainView clean. Internally it manages RtSensorDataWorker and RtSensorInterpolationMatWorker on background threads. Background Workers​ Workers implement the Producer–Consumer pattern on standard-library threads. The streaming cadence runs on a PeriodicTask (a std::jthread), interpolation-matrix recomputations run in request order on a single-thread mne::ThreadPool, and STC loading runs on its own std::jthread. The worker objects stay on the GUI thread; their results reach it through queued signal–slot connections, so heavy computation (interpolation matrix construction, per-vertex color mapping) never blocks the render loop. Worker state is guarded by std::mutex, and the controllers join their threads before the workers are destroyed. Worker Role RtSensorDataWorker Receives raw sensor samples, applies the interpolation matrix, and emits per-vertex color arrays ready for GPU upload RtSensorInterpolationMatWorker Builds the sparse interpolation matrix mapping sensor positions to surface vertices (recomputed when sensor geometry changes) RtSourceDataWorker Streams source-estimate samples and computes per-vertex STC colors RtSourceInterpolationMatWorker Builds the source-space interpolation matrix StcLoadingWorker Asynchronous STC file I/O — loads large .stc files without blocking the UI

Quick Start — Visualizing a Brain Surface​ #include <mne/viz/backends/qt/3d/view/brainview.h> #include <mne/viz/backends/qt/3d/model/braintreemodel.h> #include <mne/fs/surface.h> #include <mne/fs/annotation.h> // Create view and model BrainView *view = new BrainView(); BrainTreeModel *model = new BrainTreeModel(); view->setModel(model); // Load FreeSurfer surfaces mne::FsSurface surfLh("sample", 0, "inflated", subjectsDir); mne::FsSurface surfRh("sample", 1, "inflated", subjectsDir); model->addSurface("sample", "lh", "inflated", surfLh); model->addSurface("sample", "rh", "inflated", surfRh); // Load annotations mne::FsAnnotation annotLh("sample", 0, "aparc", subjectsDir); model->addAnnotation("sample", "lh", annotLh); view->show(); Adding a Connectivity Network​ #include <mne/viz/backends/qt/3d/model/braintreemodel.h> #include <mne/connectivity/network/network.h> // After computing connectivity (see Connectivity library docs) std::vector<Network> networks = compute_connectivity(settings); model->addNetwork(networks.first(), "PLI");

Namespace: mne::viz::qt · Library: Visualization: Qt Backend · Source: viz/backends/qt/3d/view/brainrenderer.h #include <mne/viz/backends/qt/brainrenderer.h> class mne::viz::qt::BrainRenderer BrainRenderer handles the low-level RHI rendering logic, managing pipelines, shaders, and draw calls for brain surfaces. Deprecated since 3.0.0: the brain view describes its frames with BrainFrameComposer and records them with RhiFrameRenderer. BrainRenderer will be removed in a later release. Qt RHI-based 3-D renderer managing scene objects, lighting, camera, and render pipeline for brain visualization.

Initialize resources (shaders, pipelines) for the given RHI and render pass. Ensures pipelines for all supported modes are created. Parameters: rhi : *QRhi ** Pointer to QRhi instance. rp : *QRhiRenderPassDescriptor ** Render pass descriptor. sampleCount : int MSAA sample count.

Create the dual render-target pair for multi-pass rendering. Both render targets share the same color texture and depth-stencil buffer but differ in their load/store flags: m_rtClear: clears color+depth on beginPass (first pass) m_rtPreserve: preserves previous output (passes 2+) Qt bakes these flags into native resources at create() time, so calling setFlags() dynamically does NOT work (especially on WebGL). This is the validated pattern from test_wasm_multi_pass. Parameters: rhi : *QRhi ** QRhi instance. colorTex : *QRhiTexture ** Color texture (owned by QRhiWidget or caller). pixelSize : const QSize & Render target dimensions.
Returns: *QRhiRenderTarget ** — The clearing render target (pass 1): the external target when one is set, else the own one.

Draw into a render target owned by the caller, e.g. the current target of a QRhiSwapChain, instead of the own targets built by ensureRenderTargets(). beginFrame() then clears and draws into it. Parameters: rt : *QRhiRenderTarget ** External render target, or nullptr to use the own targets again.

Start a new frame: frees all per-draw uniform slots. Call before the frame's first prepare call. A frame is recorded in two phases. First every prepare*() call writes its uniforms and uploads into resource update batches. Then beginFrame() commits them, and the issue*() calls only bind and draw: QRhi forbids resource updates inside a render pass, and prepare calls made inside one are rejected with a warning. The renderer owns the GPU copies of the renderables' streams. They are created on the first draw, updated when a stream's generation changes, and freed once the renderable is destroyed or has not been drawn for a while.
Returns: int — Number of renderables whose GPU copies the renderer currently holds.

Begin the first render pass of a frame. Clears color and depth. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer to record to. updates : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource updates to commit before the pass, or nullptr.

Begin an additional render pass that preserves previous output. Uses the internal preserving render target (m_rtPreserve). Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer. updates : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource updates to commit before the pass, or nullptr.

Upload the surface's streams if they changed and write the uniforms of one surface draw. Parameters: u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. data : const SceneData & Scene uniforms (MVP, light, etc). surface : *BrainSurface ** Pointer to surface. Returns: int — Uniform buffer offset for this draw, or -1 on failure.

Draw a surface with the uniforms from prepareSurfaceDraw(). Call inside a pass. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer. surface : *BrainSurface ** Pointer to surface to draw. mode : ShaderMode Shader mode. uniformOffset : int Offset returned by prepareSurfaceDraw().

Upload the dipoles' streams if they changed and write the uniforms of their draw. Parameters: u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. data : const SceneData & Scene uniforms. dipoles : *DipoleObject ** Pointer to DipoleObject. Returns: int — Uniform buffer offset, or -1 when nothing is drawn.

Draw dipoles as instanced cones. Call inside a pass. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer. dipoles : *DipoleObject ** Pointer to DipoleObject. uniformOffset : int Offset returned by prepareDipoleDraw().

Upload the network's streams if they changed and write the uniforms of its draws. Parameters: u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. data : const SceneData & Scene uniforms. network : *NetworkObject ** Pointer to NetworkObject. Returns: int — Uniform buffer offset, or -1 when nothing is drawn.

Draw a connectivity network: instanced node spheres and edge cylinders. Call inside a pass. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer. network : *NetworkObject ** Pointer to NetworkObject. uniformOffset : int Offset returned by prepareNetworkDraw().

Upload the polyline's streams if they changed and write the uniforms of its draw. Parameters: u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. data : const SceneData & Scene uniforms. polyline : *PolylineObject ** Pointer to PolylineObject. Returns: int — Uniform buffer offset, or -1 when nothing is drawn.

Draw a polyline as connected segments. Call inside a pass. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer. polyline : *PolylineObject ** Pointer to PolylineObject. uniformOffset : int Offset returned by preparePolylineDraw().

Upload the electrodes' streams if they changed and write the uniforms of their draws. Parameters: u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. data : const SceneData & Scene uniforms. electrodes : *ElectrodeObject ** Pointer to ElectrodeObject. Returns: int — Uniform buffer offset, or -1 when nothing is drawn.

Draw electrode lead bodies and contacts, opaque and depth-tested. Call inside a pass. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer. electrodes : *ElectrodeObject ** Pointer to ElectrodeObject. uniformOffset : int Offset returned by prepareElectrodeDraw().

Prepare live video overlay GPU resources and upload the latest frame. Must be called before a render pass starts. Texture uploads require a blit encoder on Metal and must not be recorded while a render encoder is active. Parameters: rhi : *QRhi ** QRhi pointer. u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch owned by the caller. overlay : *VideoOverlay ** Pointer to VideoOverlay; ignored when null/disabled.

Write the uniforms of one video overlay draw: a camera-facing quad at the focus position, or, with a target surface, a decal projected onto that mesh. Call after prepareVideoOverlay(). Parameters: u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. data : const SceneData & Scene uniforms (MVP, camera position). overlay : *VideoOverlay ** Pointer to VideoOverlay; ignored when null/disabled. surface : *BrainSurface ** Target surface mesh (typically scalp/head), or nullptr for the quad. Returns: int — Uniform buffer offset for this draw, or -1 when nothing is drawn.

Draw a video overlay prepared with prepareVideoOverlayDraw(). Call inside a pass. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer. overlay : *VideoOverlay ** Pointer to VideoOverlay. surface : *BrainSurface ** Same target surface as in prepareVideoOverlayDraw(). uniformOffset : int Offset returned by prepareVideoOverlayDraw().

Prepare MRI slice GPU resources and upload texture data. Must be called before a render pass starts. Creates the slice pipeline lazily on first use and uploads the slice texture. Parameters: rhi : *QRhi ** QRhi pointer. u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch owned by the caller. slice : *SliceObject ** Pointer to SliceObject; ignored when null. slotIndex : int Slot index (0=axial, 1=coronal, 2=sagittal).

Write the uniforms of one MRI slice draw into a resource update batch. Parameters: u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. data : const SceneData & Scene uniforms (MVP, camera position). slotIndex : int Slot index (0=axial, 1=coronal, 2=sagittal). Returns: int — Uniform buffer offset for this draw, or -1 on failure.

Draw an MRI slice prepared with prepareSliceDraw(). Call inside a pass. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer (must be inside a render pass). slotIndex : int Slot index matching the prepareSliceDraw call. uniformOffset : int Offset returned by prepareSliceDraw().
End any render pass (clearing or preserving). Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer.

Upload a screen-space overlay (text labels, pane separators) that issueScreenOverlayDraw() blends over the whole render target. The texture is re-uploaded only when the image changed. Parameters: rhi : *QRhi ** QRhi instance. u : *QRhiResourceUpdateBatch ** Resource update batch, committed before the pass. overlay : const QImage & Premultiplied RGBA image of the target's pixel size; a null image draws nothing.
Alpha-blend the overlay uploaded by prepareScreenOverlay() over the whole render target. Call inside the pass, after the 3-D scene. Parameters: cb : *QRhiCommandBuffer ** Command buffer.
Returns: bool — Whether the last prepareScreenOverlay() call left an overlay to draw.

Namespace: mne::viz · Source: src/libs/mne/viz mne_viz (namespace mne::viz, src/libs/mne/viz) describes what the MNE-CPP viewers show and how they behave, without a GUI toolkit or a GPU. Backends under src/libs/mne/viz/backends/ render and host it; mne_viz_qt is the Qt backend. Folder Contents figures/ Figures as display lists (Canvas, line, bar, butterfly, image, spline and vector plots, sensor and average layouts, ticks, colour maps), rendered to SVG (SvgRenderer) or images (RasterRenderer) views/ The logic of the interactive views: TraceView with its buffers, geometry, markers and animation, the brain view's OrbitCamera, picking, pane layout, interaction and overlay, and toolkit-neutral input events gpu/ GpuFrame, a backend-neutral description of a GPU frame (buffers, pipelines, draw calls); TraceFrameBuilder and BrainFrameBuilder produce it and the built-in SoftwareRenderer executes it headless forms/ SettingsForm, the description of a settings panel from which a backend builds its widgets models/ View models: ChannelTable, SpectrumTable, BidsTree, evoked conditions A backend depends on mne_viz only, never on another backend, and mne_viz never includes from backends/; the dependency audit enforces both. Only the Qt backend uses Qt. target_link_libraries(my_tool PRIVATE mne_viz)

Namespace: mne::viz · Library: Visualization Library · Source: viz/views/brain_view_interaction.h #include <mne/viz/brain_view_interaction.h> class mne::viz::BrainViewInteraction Input state machine of the 3-D brain view. Drags follow the buttons held according to the pointer events. In the single view a left-button drag orbits the camera; in the multi view it orbits the perspective pane under the pointer and pans the other panes, and dragging a splitter resizes the panes. The wheel zooms the view (or the pane) under the pointer, R resets the rotation of the single view and S asks for a snapshot. A left click without a drag reports the clicked point, a hover move the hovered point. The camera states are owned by the host (attach_cameras()); the host keeps the pane setup up to date with set_view_size() and set_panes() before it forwards events. Effects go out through Effects; positions are rounded to whole logical pixels, as pane hit-testing is done in pixels.

Namespace: mne::viz · Library: Visualization Library · Source: viz/panels/form_view.h #include <mne/viz/form_view.h> class mne::viz::FormView Shows and edits a SettingsForm in a Surface, drawn toolkit-free in the look of a Theme. The title of the form comes first, then each group as a card with one row per visible field: the label on the left, the editor on the right. Bool fields are switches, numbers steppers with - and + buttons (the wheel steps too), choices cycle with < and > buttons, text, path and directory fields are line edits, actions buttons, colours swatches and info fields toned text. The item lists of a panel fill their custom fields as list boxes: a click selects, Ctrl or Cmd extends the selection of multi-selection lists, the wheel scrolls them, the arrow keys move the selection and Delete removes the selected items of removable lists. Disabled fields are greyed and ignore input. The view follows the form: it lays out again when fields are added, removed or relabelled and repaints when values change. Content taller than the surface scrolls with the wheel. scdcInterpolationMat Computes geodesic distances (SCDC) and builds the sparse interpolation matrix in a single pass, without allocating a dense nVertices x nSources distance table. Namespace: mne::viz · Library: Visualization Library · Source: viz/brain/realtime/rtsensordataworker.h #include <mne/viz/rtsensordataworker.h> class mne::viz::RtSensorDataWorker RtSensorDataWorker processes incoming sensor measurement data in a background thread. It manages a data queue, performs averaging, applies a dense mapping matrix (MEG or EEG sensor → surface vertex), normalises values symmetrically, and converts them to per-vertex ABGR colours for rendering. This worker is driven by a timer in the RtSensorDataController and follows the same architecture as RtSourceDataWorker, adapted for dense sensor-to-surface mapping instead of sparse source interpolation. Background worker for real-time sensor data streaming.

Add a new sensor measurement vector to the streaming queue. The vector contains one measurement per picked sensor channel. Parameters: data : const Eigen::VectorXf & Sensor measurement vector (nChannels x 1).
Clear all queued data and reset averaging state.

Set the dense mapping matrix (sensor → surface vertices). This matrix is typically produced by mne::FwdFieldMap::computeMegMapping() or computeEegMapping(). Size: (nVertices × nChannels). Parameters: surfaceKey : const std::string & Key of the surface the matrix maps onto; colours are emitted for it. mat : std::shared_ptr< Eigen::MatrixXf > Dense mapping matrix.
Set the number of samples to average before emitting. Parameters: numAvr : int Number of averages (1 = no averaging).
Set the colormap type used for color conversion. Parameters: name : const std::string & Colormap name ("MNE", "Hot", "Jet", "Viridis", "Cool", "RedBlue").

Set explicit normalization thresholds instead of auto-normalization. When set, the symmetric auto-normalization is replaced by fixed thresholds. Values below min are mapped to 0, above max to 1. Pass min == 0 and max == 0 to re-enable auto-normalization. Parameters: min : double Lower threshold (values below are at colormap start). max : double Upper threshold (values above are at colormap end).

Namespace: mne::viz · Library: Visualization Library · Source: viz/brain/realtime/rtsensorinterpolationmatworker.h #include <mne/viz/rtsensorinterpolationmatworker.h> class mne::viz::RtSensorInterpolationMatWorker RtSensorInterpolationMatWorker computes dense sensor-to-surface field-mapping matrices in a background thread. This worker encapsulates the expensive mne::FwdFieldMap::computeMegMapping() and computeEegMapping() calls that were previously performed synchronously on the main thread inside BrainView::buildSensorFieldMapping(). The worker stores all relevant parameters (evoked info, surface geometry, transforms, etc.) and recomputes the mapping matrices when any parameter changes. It emits newMappingMatrixAvailable() when a new matrix is ready. Thread-safety: all public setters are mutex-protected and schedule a recomputation via the computeMapping() slot. Namespace: mne::viz · Library: Visualization Library · Source: viz/brain/sensorfieldmapper.h #include <mne/viz/sensorfieldmapper.h> class mne::viz::SensorFieldMapper Encapsulates sensor-to-surface field mapping for MEG and EEG sensors. This class owns the mapping state (evoked data, mapping matrices, channel picks, contour prefixes, surface key references) and provides methods to build mapping matrices and apply them to produce per-vertex field colours and iso-contour meshes. The class operates on surface and contour surfaces stored in the caller's surface map. It reads from / writes to those surfaces but does not own them, keeping ownership in the BrainView. Compute the normalization range anchored at the peak-GFP time. For each modality the Global Field Power (GFP = sqrt(mean(V_i^2))) is evaluated across all time samples and we pick the time of maximum GFP. vmax = max(|mapped|) is then computed at that peak time, giving the colour-map range [-vmax, +vmax]. This matches MNE-Python's plot_field behaviour, where the initial view shows the evoked peak, so the colour scale is anchored to it. The range stays fixed during time scrubbing until explicitly recomputed (e.g. by switching to a new evoked data set). Must be called after building or reusing a mapping matrix with new evoked data. buildMapping() calls this automatically.

Fit a sphere to the digitization headshape points. Replicates MNE-Python's fit_sphere_to_headshape (linear least- squares sphere fit). Uses FIFFV_POINT_EXTRA digitization points by default; falls back to EXTRA + EEG if fewer than 4 extra points exist. Nose/face points (z < 0 && y > 0) are excluded. Namespace: mne::viz · Library: Visualization Library · Source: viz/views/view_animator.h #include <mne/viz/view_animator.h> class mne::viz::ViewAnimator Runs the scroll and zoom animations a TraceView asks for, without timers. The host starts the animations from the view's animate_scroll and animate_zoom effects, stops the scroll animation on stop_animations, and calls tick() with the current time for every frame (or from a timer) while it returns true. Animations use the cubic ease-out curve f(t) = 1 - (1 - t)^3, whose initial speed is three times the mean speed: an inertial glide of duration T over a distance v T / 3 starts at speed v. There is at most one scroll animation (a requested scroll or an inertial glide) and one zoom animation; starting one replaces the running one of its kind.

MNE Analyze uses the Model/View architecture from Qt to separate data storage from presentation. All data — FIFF files, annotations, averages — is represented as a model that views can display. This guide explains how to create a new data model for a custom data type.

┌──────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ │ Data Loader │────►│ Data Manager │────►│ Views │ │ (loads files) │ │ (stores models) │ │ (display models) │ └──────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ │ ┌──────▼──────┐ │ AbstractModel│ │ (your new │ │ subclass) │ └─────────────┘ All data models inherit from AbstractModel, which itself extends QAbstractItemModel. The DataLoader reads files from disk and creates model instances, while the DataManager (via AnalyzeData) stores and manages them. Plugins access models through the event system.
AbstractModel is located at src/apps/mne_analyze/libs/anShared/Model/abstractmodel.h. Since it extends QAbstractItemModel, you must implement all pure virtual functions from both classes.

getType()​ Returns the type identifier for your model. Add a new entry to the MODEL_TYPE enum in src/apps/mne_analyze/libs/anShared/Utils/types.h: enum MODEL_TYPE { ANSHAREDLIB_FIFFRAW_MODEL, ANSHAREDLIB_ANNOTATION_MODEL, ANSHAREDLIB_AVERAGING_MODEL, ANSHAREDLIB_MYDATA_MODEL, // ← add your type here }; Then implement: MODEL_TYPE MyDataModel::getType() const { return MODEL_TYPE::ANSHAREDLIB_MYDATA_MODEL; } data()​ Returns data for a given model index and role. This is the primary function that views call to retrieve displayable content: QVariant MyDataModel::data(const QModelIndex& index, int role) const { if (!index.isValid()) return QVariant(); if (role == Qt::DisplayRole) { // Return data based on row and column return m_data.at(index.row()).at(index.column()); } return QVariant(); } flags()​ Returns item flags (selectable, editable, enabled, etc.): Qt::ItemFlags MyDataModel::flags(const QModelIndex& index) const { if (!index.isValid()) return Qt::NoItemFlags; return Qt::ItemIsEnabled | Qt::ItemIsSelectable; } index()​ Creates and returns a QModelIndex for the given row, column, and parent: QModelIndex MyDataModel::index(int row, int column, const QModelIndex& parent) const { Q_UNUSED(parent) if (row < 0 || row >= rowCount() || column < 0 || column >= columnCount()) return QModelIndex(); return createIndex(row, column); } parent()​ Returns the parent index. For flat (non-hierarchical) models, return an empty index: QModelIndex MyDataModel::parent(const QModelIndex& index) const { Q_UNUSED(index) return QModelIndex(); } rowCount()​ Returns the number of rows. The meaning depends on your data — for example, the FiffRawViewModel returns the number of channels: int MyDataModel::rowCount(const QModelIndex& parent) const { Q_UNUSED(parent) return m_data.size(); } columnCount()​ Returns the number of columns: int MyDataModel::columnCount(const QModelIndex& parent) const { Q_UNUSED(parent) return m_iNumColumns; }

If your model supports saving data back to disk, override saveToFile() from AbstractModel: bool MyDataModel::saveToFile(const QString& sPath) { QFile file(sPath); if (!file.open(QIODevice::WriteOnly)) { mne::Log::warning("[MyDataModel::saveToFile] Could not open {}", sPath.toStdString()); return false; } // Write your data format // ... return true; }

To allow users to load your data type from a file: In DataLoader::loadFilePath(), add support for your file extension so that the file dialog recognizes it. In the load handler, create a new instance of your model and pass it to the data manager.

To create a model from within a plugin (e.g., computed results rather than files): In AnalyzeData.h, extend addModel() to handle your MODEL_TYPE. Specify the data type your model corresponds to — see bidsviewmodel.h for the available types, or add a new one.
To support saving, ensure your file extension is included in DataLoader::onSaveFilePressed(), and implement saveToFile() in your model.

// mydatamodel.h #pragma once #include "../Utils/types.h" #include "abstractmodel.h" class MyDataModel : public mne::analyze::AbstractModel { Q_OBJECT public: MyDataModel(const QList<QStringList>& data, QObject* parent = nullptr); // AbstractModel MODEL_TYPE getType() const override; // QAbstractItemModel QVariant data(const QModelIndex& index, int role) const override; Qt::ItemFlags flags(const QModelIndex& index) const override; QModelIndex index(int row, int col, const QModelIndex& parent = QModelIndex()) const override; QModelIndex parent(const QModelIndex& index) const override; int rowCount(const QModelIndex& parent = QModelIndex()) const override; int columnCount(const QModelIndex& parent = QModelIndex()) const override; private: QList<QStringList> m_data; }; // mydatamodel.cpp #include "mydatamodel.h" MyDataModel::MyDataModel(const QList<QStringList>& data, QObject* parent) : AbstractModel(parent) , m_data(data) { } MODEL_TYPE MyDataModel::getType() const { return MODEL_TYPE::ANSHAREDLIB_MYDATA_MODEL; } QVariant MyDataModel::data(const QModelIndex& index, int role) const { if (!index.isValid() || role != Qt::DisplayRole) return QVariant(); return m_data.at(index.row()).at(index.column()); } Qt::ItemFlags MyDataModel::flags(const QModelIndex& index) const { return index.isValid() ? (Qt::ItemIsEnabled | Qt::ItemIsSelectable) : Qt::NoItemFlags; } QModelIndex MyDataModel::index(int row, int col, const QModelIndex& parent) const { Q_UNUSED(parent) return createIndex(row, col); } QModelIndex MyDataModel::parent(const QModelIndex& index) const { Q_UNUSED(index) return QModelIndex(); } int MyDataModel::rowCount(const QModelIndex& parent) const { Q_UNUSED(parent) return m_data.size(); } int MyDataModel::columnCount(const QModelIndex& parent) const { Q_UNUSED(parent) return m_data.isEmpty() ? 0 : m_data.first().size(); }

Once registered, your plugin can create and display the model: // In your plugin's handleEvent() or a load function: QList<QStringList> data = parseMyFile(sFilePath); auto pModel = QSharedPointer<MyDataModel>::create(data); // Notify MNE Analyze about the new model via the event system QVariant varModel = QVariant::fromValue(pModel); m_pCommu->publishEvent(EVENT_TYPE::NEW_MODEL_AVAILABLE, varModel); Views that are subscribed to NEW_MODEL_AVAILABLE will then receive and display the model.
